{"content": "1|---
2|name: skill-amend-specs
3|description: Evidence-first amendment workflow. Use when revising a block, spec, plan, or ADR after review findings or change requests.
4|source: canon
5|canon_version: HEAD
6|---
7|
8|# Skill: Amend Specifications
9|
10|Use this skill when amending a block, spec, plan, or ADR that a reviewer returned with change
11|requests. You are editing a **contract**, not code: its job is to be unambiguous and true.
12|
13|## The four that break amendments
14|
15|**1. Do not widen the scope.** The amendment answers findings. It adds no criteria, pulls in no adjacent work, promotes no "while we're here" idea. A finding that cannot be resolved inside the current scope is an escalation, not a licence to widen. Do not quietly *narrow* it either: an acceptance criterion may not be downgraded to a weaker verification method (`test:` → `manual_by:`, `cmd:` → code review) to make a finding go away. Renegotiating a criterion needs the operator's approval recorded in the document.
16|
17|**2. Not every finding is correct.** A reviewer asked to find gaps will report some, sound work or not, and obeying all of them mechanically is how a spec bloats. Each finding is either **RESOLVED**, **DISPUTED** (state your evidence), or **ESCALATED** (state what you need). Disputing with evidence is the expected move, not an act of insubordination; capitulating without new evidence is a defect.
18|
19|**3. Verify before you write, not after.** Every fact the amendment rests on gets re-read at its source: the code (`file:line`), or the provider's *current* documentation (URL + the date you read it). Facts from memory, from your own earlier draft, or from the reviewer's prose are stale until re-read. Training data is not evidence. There is nothing here to run red, so guessing costs a full review cycle.
20|
21|**4. The spec holds implementation only.** No review history, no round numbers, no finding IDs, no justification of an earlier draft, no meta-commentary. That belongs in the ledger. The amended document must not be longer than the one you started from. Anything else needs the operator asking for it, in writing.
22|
23|## Working
24|
25|Read the current document end to end first, on disk, not as you remember it. Then the findings in full, including the ones you intend to dispute.
26|
27|Keep a ledger, one row per finding: what is claimed, what you will change, where, and the evidence. A finding you cannot restate in your own words, ask about.
28|
29|Evidence means pasted output. Every command, path, line number and count the amendment asserts gets run or read first, and its actual result — including the exit code, for a command — goes in the ledger next to the claim it supports. Write the command into the document only after its output is in the ledger, and only in the form you ran it: same flags, same repository, same working directory. A command that errored, or that returns nothing where the criterion needs something to read, is not ready to be written down.
30|
31|**Cite only what you just printed.** Every line range, every count, and every claim that spans a set ("all", "each", "every", "the only") is the pasted, unelided output of a command you ran in this pass. A citation you did not open in this pass is a guess with a colon in it.
32|
33|Fix the class, not the sentence quoted. If one ambiguous criterion is flagged and three siblings share the ambiguity, fix all four and say so.
34|
35|Change nothing a finding did not name. Spot something real, log it as a new finding for the operator to triage.
36|
37|Text adjacent to your edit that your amendment makes wrong is now your defect, whoever wrote it.
38|
39|## Before you call it done
40|
41|Re-read the **whole** document, not the diff. Patch-wise editing reliably leaves the paragraph you fixed agreeing with itself and contradicting a section three pages away. Sweep every claim at its source while you are in there, not only the ones a finding named: an untouched sentence can have been wrong from the start, and what the sweep turns up you fix in the same pass.
42|
43|Open every cross-reference you touched or added. Each must exist and say what you claim. Do not trust a reference's own label.
44|
45|Check the document against its template: required sections present, a verification method declared for every acceptance criterion, header fields intact.
46|
47|Then report: what changed, which finding it answers, the status of every ledger row, every assumption, and everything you could not verify. Unverified reported plainly is fine. Unverified reported as settled is not.", "total_lines": 47, "file_size": 4481, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false, "not_found": false}

{"content": "1|# Pi model-logo contract
2|
3|**Verdict: READY.** Implementation and deployment require separate authorization.
4|
5|Card: `42L-2130`. Repository: `4242labs/herdr-radar-plus`.
6|Compatibility baseline: Radar `0.42.0`, native Pi `1.0.4`, Herdr `0.9.1`; Darkseid/macOS and Alghul/Linux.
7|
8|## 1. Problem, goal and authority
9|
10|Radar already renders a model-family mark beside the agent mark. Its title-based model lookup cannot reliably identify Pi's selected model. The goal is to show the family of Pi's actual selected model beside Pi's agent logo on both named hosts, or no model mark when the model cannot be established. Preserve Pi's terminal title, session/project naming, existing Hermes behavior and the managed Herdr lifecycle integration.
11|
12|The operator owns implementation, deployment, activation and live model-selection authorization. The implementing engineer owns the producer, Pi-only consumer, tests and runbook; the authorized deployer owns host preflight, source readback and rollback. Pi owns model selection and terminal titles; the managed Herdr integration owns lifecycle/session reporting; Herdr owns pane identity and token storage; Radar alone owns rendered model glyphs.
13|
14|Current authority is contract/evidence amendment only. Do not implement, install, upgrade, reload, restart, change a live model, submit a prompt, modify credentials, dispatch reviewers or merge on the strength of this document.
15|
16|## 2. Scope, dependencies and flow
17|
18|In scope: one standalone global native-Pi extension; a narrowly scoped metadata consumer in Radar; reuse of the existing model-family keys, glyphs, sidebar cells, scheduler and token-write pipeline; automated feature/regression tests; two-host deployment and rollback procedures. No new service or dependency.
19|
20|Out of scope: terminal-title transport or interception; modifying Pi internals or `herdr-agent-state.ts`; adopting the community integration wholesale; changing Hermes/other harnesses; font, palette or sidebar redesign; providers, authentication, upgrades, inference, Telegram/bots, Night Watch, Windows, other hosts, new live Pi sessions and service/Pi restarts.
21|
22|Existing interfaces: `lib/state.js` obtains agents and their tokens, composes rows and publishes `model`/`model_stale`; `lib/logos.js` owns family lookup and glyphs; `lib/managed-config.js` already puts model cells after agent cells. Modify the Pi branch only, retaining the legacy non-Pi lookup. The prospective extension artifact is `extensions/pi-model-logo.js`; deliver it beside the managed extension, never over it. README/CHANGELOG receive only feature behavior, activation, troubleshooting and rollback instructions when implementation is authorized.
23|
24|Prerequisites: supported Pi public lifecycle/model/session getters; Herdr token patches, TTL, sequence numbers and authoritative session references; a native interactive Pi pane with its managed lifecycle integration; active Radar model cells with matching glyph variant. Deployment must verify these immediately before mutation. A failed prerequisite blocks that host without repairing unrelated configuration.
25|
26|Happy path: native Pi `session_start` reads the current selected ID and session reference; the extension publishes distinct input tokens; Radar validates the current Pi occupant and reference, resolves the ID to an existing family, and publishes its usual model glyph tokens. Herdr renders them beside the existing Pi mark. Model selection replaces the inputs; unknown selection clears the model cells. Pi's own later title writes do not participate in this flow.
27|
28|Assumptions used as execution facts: none. Live configuration, token capacity and activation safety are explicit preflight gates, not claimed passes. API availability is not live rendering acceptance.
29|
30|## 3. Input, ownership and transport contract
31|
32|### Token ownership
33|
34|| Key | Writer | Value | Expiry |
35||---|---|---|---|
36|| `pi_model_id` | New Pi extension only | Exact selected `ctx.model.id`, or JSON null | `ttl_ms: 60000` |
37|| `pi_model_ref` | New Pi extension only | Lowercase SHA256 reference digest, or JSON null | Same report and TTL as ID |
38|| `model`, `model_stale` | Radar only | Existing family glyph or null | Existing Radar behavior |
39|
40|Use the single fixed metadata source `user:radar-pi-model`; never create a source per reload/session. Input tokens are not sidebar cells and are not Radar-owned cleanup keys. Token sources are not separate namespaces. Do not write `title`, `display_agent`, state labels, lifecycle state, session authority or resume commands. Do not write model output keys from Pi.
41|
42|For the selected ID, require a nonempty string with no whitespace or C0/C1 control characters and at most 80 Unicode scalar values. Do not trim, normalize, truncate or substitute a provider/display name. Invalid, missing or overlength ID becomes null. A valid unrecognized ID may travel unchanged; it resolves to no family.
43|
44|Reference construction follows the managed native integration: use a nonempty absolute `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionFile()` first with kind `path`; otherwise a nonempty `getSessionId()` with kind `id`. Do not read a session file. Hash UTF-8 bytes of `kind + U+0000 + value` with Node's built-in SHA256. Never transmit or persist the unhashed reference. If neither accessor provides a valid reference, clear both ID and reference instead of reusing a prior session. A failed model getter produces a null ID. This digest is a correlation guard, not authentication against another local process able to forge tokens.
45|
46|### Serialization and sequence recovery
47|
48|Use built-in `node:net`, `node:crypto`, `node:fs` and `node:path`, not a Radar import or subprocess. Environment gating requires `HERDR_ENV === '1'`, nonempty `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, nonempty `HERDR_PANE_ID`, and `ctx.mode === 'tui'`. Never guess a socket/pane or use the currently focused pane. Send newline-delimited JSON to the supplied local socket. Each request has a distinct ID, a 1000ms deadline, complete-line JSON/error validation, and socket destruction on completion/error/timeout. Limit a reply buffer to 1 MiB; partial, excessive or malformed replies fail the operation. No CLI fallback or external HTTP/provider call.
49|
50|The write envelope is `{id, method: "pane.report_metadata", params: {pane_id, source, seq, tokens, ttl_ms}}`, with the pinned environment pane ID, fixed source above, reserved numeric sequence, exactly the two input token keys, and `ttl_ms: 60000`. Serialize to UTF-8 JSON plus one newline; omit presentation/lifecycle fields. Readback uses `{id, method: "pane.get", params: {pane_id}}` with the same pinned ID. Require the matching string response ID, an object `result` and no `error`; pane readback additionally requires `result.type === "pane_info"`, the matching `result.pane.pane_id`, and its `tokens` map. A null patch succeeds only when that key is absent on readback. Never use a focused-pane default.
51|
52|Maintain one session generation and one serialized drain. Retain at most one latest pending snapshot; model events supersede older pending values. A callback from a retired generation cannot read context or initiate another request. Capture plain values before asynchronous work; never read an invalidated context.
53|
54|Keep a durable counter independent of Herdr's ephemeral tokens. Its prospective directory is `pi-model-logo-state` beside the global native `extensions` directory. Its filename is the lowercase SHA256 of UTF-8 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH + U+0000 + HERDR_PANE_ID`, followed by `.json`; its sole content is `{"last":N}`. Require N to be a nonnegative JavaScript safe integer. Initial-install preflight provisions zero before activation only with release evidence that this source has never published for that socket/pane; token absence is not that evidence. Otherwise preserve the existing counter or stop. Runtime never initializes a missing counter. Cap reads at 64 bytes. Directory/file modes are 0700/0600, with current-user ownership and no symlink traversal. Corrupt, foreign-owned, symlinked, missing, unwritable or exhausted state stops publication with a generic warning; it is never silently reset. No session reference, title or transcript enters this store. Preflight forbids multiple producer processes for the same socket/pane. Within one process, serialize counter updates across reload generations using a process-scoped registry; retire old generation work before a new generation can publish. No lock file or wall-clock seed.
55|
56|For each update, including refresh and clearing:
57|
58|1. Read the owned counter, choose N = last + 1, and require N to be a safe integer. Persist `{"last":N}` to an exclusively created same-directory temporary file, sync and close it, then atomically rename it over the counter before any IPC write. Remove only this operation's own temporary file on failure. If persistence fails, send nothing. Read back the reserved counter before proceeding.
59|2. Report ID and reference together with source `user:radar-pi-model`, `seq: N` and `ttl_ms: 60000`. Clear both with null for shutdown or unavailable reference; clear ID alone for an unavailable model when the reference remains valid. Every attempt reserves a fresh number, including retries and cleanup.
60|3. Read back the pinned pane's inputs before acknowledging success; an API success may be an ignored old sequence. If a newer desired snapshot arrived, drain that snapshot next; do not resend the superseded one. Failure leaves only the latest desired snapshot pending for the next trigger.
61|
62|Persist-before-send allows skipped numbers after failure but prevents reuse after a process crash, reload, lease expiry, server restart between requests, or wall-clock change. Server token loss cannot erase the counter. Preserve counters during shutdown and rollback so same-pane reinstall remains safe; do not delete/reset them while the server can retain this source's sequence history. They are invisible feature-owned state, not sidebar tokens. Cleanup is allowed only after separately verifying that the pane lifetime has ended. Never allocate another sequence source to bypass a refusal. The reservation precedes the IPC request even if shutdown reaches its deadline; no unreserved clear may be sent.
63|
64|### Lifecycle, expiry and recovery
65|
66|The factory registers handlers only; it starts no sockets, processes or timers. `session_start` first retires old generation resources, then initializes eligible native TUI state, publishes fresh values and starts one unrefed 30000ms metadata-refresh timer. `model_select` publishes freshly read current values immediately; restoration uses `session_start`, not a presumed restore-sourced model event. Startup/reload/new/resume/fork all reinitialize from the supplied current context. Rename does not affect the model/reference or call a title API.
67|
68|The refresh is a metadata lease renewal, not terminal-title reconciliation: there are zero title writes. It republishes fresh values even if unchanged, so server token loss is recoverable without a prompt/restart. Recovery occurs on the next event or refresh after the same socket/pane becomes reachable and its authoritative Pi reference is available; no absolute wall-clock SLA under event-loop stalls is promised. If the reference is absent/mismatched, Radar remains blank until the existing integration establishes it. If the pane no longer exists, retire the publisher and its timer; never redirect to another pane. Changed socket/pane environment requires later separately authorized idle reload, not discovery or restart.
69|
70|On `session_shutdown`, retire generation/timer first, cancel outstanding sockets, discard old pending updates, and attempt the serialized null patch from captured data. Bound cleanup to 4000ms in total and destroy its sockets at that deadline. If clearing fails, the last successful ID/ref expires after its 60000ms lease; then Radar clears the model cells on its next successful frame. Leave Pi usable and the managed lifecycle integration untouched. Repeated shutdown is idempotent. Warn at most once per generation using generic text without identifiers, references, names, stack traces or payloads.
71|
72|Transient socket/server failure gets no tight retry loop: retain only the latest desired snapshot and retry on the next model/session trigger or scheduled refresh. Do not mark a failed or ignored write delivered. A valid empty agent list is not a failed list read: preserve Radar's existing failed-read semantics. No stale model cache or title/provider fallback is added.
73|
74|## 4. Pi-only consumer and family resolution
75|
76|In `lib/state.js`, carry the authoritative agent/session information and input tokens through the snapshot to row composition. For a resolved Pi entry, accept inputs only when the raw authoritative agent is `pi`, `agent_session.agent` is `pi`, session source is `herdr:pi`, kind is `path` or `id`, and the digest of its nonempty exact value equals `pi_model_ref`. Missing, expired, malformed or foreign data yields no model family. Do not mistake metadata `agent`/`applies_to_source` for token guards; enforcement is in this consumer.
77|
78|For Pi, never use terminal title, project/session names, provider or the old output token to find a model. Revalidate the input ID without repairing it. Select the final nonempty slash-delimited ID component; a trailing slash is unknown. Match case-insensitive ASCII aliases anchored at the identifier start. Alias boundary is end, digit, hyphen, dot or underscore; the reasoning alias `o[1-9]` allows end, hyphen, dot or underscore, not another digit. Exactly one family may match, otherwise return null.
79|
80|| Existing family key | Identifier-start aliases | Positive fixtures | Negative fixtures |
81||---|---|---|---|
82|| claude | claude, opus, sonnet, haiku, fable | claude-sonnet-4; anthropic/claude-opus-4 | my-claude; claudelike |

1|# Contributing
2|
3|Bug reports, questions and pull requests are all welcome. Open an
4|[issue](https://github.com/4242labs/herdr-radar-plus/issues/new) for the first two.
5|
6|## Where a change belongs
7|
8|This repo is [herdr-radar](https://github.com/hhdebb/herdr-radar) plus a small set of features:
9|the attention view, named groups, groups across machines, the model mark and the machine row.
10|A fix to anything else, such as vendor logos, state marks, the settings popup or the font, is
11|better sent upstream. It reaches this repo when upstream is merged in, and every herdr-radar user
12|gets it too.
13|
14|The plus features live in:
15|
16|| File | What |
17||:--|:--|
18|| `lib/lanes.js` | Group store, presence, divider ownership. Self-test: `node lib/lanes.js` |
19|| `bin/lane.js` | The `lane-up` / `lane-down` actions |
20|| `bin/lane-sync.js` | Hub and spoke sync over SSH |
21|| `lib/frame.js` | `laneLayout`, `laneJobs`: dividers, gaps, indents |
22|| `lib/view.js` | The `attention` sort |
23|| `lib/logos.js` | `modelFor`, the model families |
24|| `lib/state.js`, `lib/managed-config.js` | Model and machine tokens and their sidebar cells |
25|
26|## Working on it
27|
28|```sh
29|npm ci
30|npm run check     # identity, vendor roster, font and README invariants
31|npm test          # node --test
32|npm run prove     # the checks above can still fail
33|npm run format    # prettier
34|node lib/lanes.js # group store self-test
35|```
36|
37|Link a checkout into Herdr to try a change live:
38|
39|```sh
40|herdr plugin link .
41|herdr plugin action invoke 4242labs.herdr-radar-plus.state-stop
42|herdr plugin action invoke 4242labs.herdr-radar-plus.state-start
43|```
44|
45|## Pull requests
46|
47|- One change per pull request, with CI green.
48|- Conventional Commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`.
49|- Say which of the plus features it touches, or that it touches none.
50|
51|## Licence of contributions
52|
53|By submitting a pull request you agree that your contribution is licensed under the same MIT
54|terms as the rest of the project. See [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md).

{"content": "1|# Pi model-logo contract
2|
3|**Verdict: READY.** Implementation and deployment require separate authorization.
4|
5|Card: `42L-2130`. Repository: `4242labs/herdr-radar-plus`.
6|Compatibility baseline: Radar `0.42.0`, native Pi `1.0.4`, Herdr `0.9.1`; Darkseid/macOS and Alghul/Linux.
7|
8|## 1. Problem, goal and authority
9|
10|Radar already renders a model-family mark beside the agent mark. Its title-based model lookup cannot reliably identify Pi's selected model. The goal is to show the family of Pi's actual selected model beside Pi's agent logo on both named hosts, or no model mark when the model cannot be established. Preserve Pi's terminal title, session/project naming, existing Hermes behavior and the managed Herdr lifecycle integration.
11|
12|The operator owns implementation, deployment, activation and live model-selection authorization. The implementing engineer owns the producer, Pi-only consumer, tests and runbook; the authorized deployer owns host preflight, source readback and rollback. Pi owns model selection and terminal titles; the managed Herdr integration owns lifecycle/session reporting; Herdr owns pane identity and token storage; Radar alone owns rendered model glyphs.
13|
14|Current authority is contract/evidence amendment only. Do not implement, install, upgrade, reload, restart, change a live model, submit a prompt, modify credentials, dispatch reviewers or merge on the strength of this document.
15|
16|## 2. Scope, dependencies and flow
17|
18|In scope: one standalone global native-Pi extension; a narrowly scoped metadata consumer in Radar; reuse of the existing model-family keys, glyphs, sidebar cells, scheduler and token-write pipeline; automated feature/regression tests; two-host deployment and rollback procedures. No new service or dependency.
19|
20|Out of scope: terminal-title transport or interception; modifying Pi internals or `herdr-agent-state.ts`; adopting the community integration wholesale; changing Hermes/other harnesses; font, palette or sidebar redesign; providers, authentication, upgrades, inference, Telegram/bots, Night Watch, Windows, other hosts, new live Pi sessions and service/Pi restarts.
21|
22|Existing interfaces: `lib/state.js` obtains agents and their tokens, composes rows and publishes `model`/`model_stale`; `lib/logos.js` owns family lookup and glyphs; `lib/managed-config.js` already puts model cells after agent cells. Modify the Pi branch only, retaining the legacy non-Pi lookup. The prospective extension artifact is `extensions/pi-model-logo.js`; deliver it beside the managed extension, never over it. README/CHANGELOG receive only feature behavior, activation, troubleshooting and rollback instructions when implementation is authorized.
23|
24|Prerequisites: supported Pi public lifecycle/model/session getters; Herdr token patches, TTL, sequence numbers and authoritative session references; a native interactive Pi pane with its managed lifecycle integration; active Radar model cells with matching glyph variant. Deployment must verify these immediately before mutation. A failed prerequisite blocks that host without repairing unrelated configuration.
25|
26|Happy path: native Pi `session_start` reads the current selected ID and session reference; the extension publishes distinct input tokens; Radar validates the current Pi occupant and reference, resolves the ID to an existing family, and publishes its usual model glyph tokens. Herdr renders them beside the existing Pi mark. Model selection replaces the inputs; unknown selection clears the model cells. Pi's own later title writes do not participate in this flow.
27|
28|Assumptions used as execution facts: none. Live configuration, token capacity and activation safety are explicit preflight gates, not claimed passes. API availability is not live rendering acceptance.
29|
30|## 3. Input, ownership and transport contract
31|
32|### Token ownership
33|
34|| Key | Writer | Value | Expiry |
35||---|---|---|---|
36|| `pi_model_id` | New Pi extension only | Exact selected `ctx.model.id`, or JSON null | `ttl_ms: 60000` |
37|| `pi_model_ref` | New Pi extension only | Lowercase SHA256 reference digest, or JSON null | Same report and TTL as ID |
38|| `model`, `model_stale` | Radar only | Existing family glyph or null | Existing Radar behavior |
39|
40|Use the single fixed metadata source `user:radar-pi-model`; never create a source per reload/session. Input tokens are not sidebar cells and are not Radar-owned cleanup keys. Token sources are not separate namespaces. Do not write `title`, `display_agent`, state labels, lifecycle state, session authority or resume commands. Do not write model output keys from Pi.
41|
42|For the selected ID, require a nonempty string with no whitespace or C0/C1 control characters and at most 80 Unicode scalar values. Do not trim, normalize, truncate or substitute a provider/display name. Invalid, missing or overlength ID becomes null. A valid unrecognized ID may travel unchanged; it resolves to no family.
43|
44|Reference construction follows the managed native integration: use a nonempty absolute `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionFile()` first with kind `path`; otherwise a nonempty `getSessionId()` with kind `id`. Do not read a session file. Hash UTF-8 bytes of `kind + U+0000 + value` with Node's built-in SHA256. Never transmit or persist the unhashed reference. If neither accessor provides a valid reference, clear both ID and reference instead of reusing a prior session. A failed model getter produces a null ID. This digest is a correlation guard, not authentication against another local process able to forge tokens.
45|
46|### Serialization and sequence recovery
47|
48|Use built-in `node:net`, `node:crypto`, `node:fs` and `node:path`, not a Radar import or subprocess. Environment gating requires `HERDR_ENV === '1'`, nonempty `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, nonempty `HERDR_PANE_ID`, and `ctx.mode === 'tui'`. Never guess a socket/pane or use the currently focused pane. Send newline-delimited JSON to the supplied local socket. Each request has a distinct ID, a 1000ms deadline, complete-line JSON/error validation, and socket destruction on completion/error/timeout. Limit a reply buffer to 1 MiB; partial, excessive or malformed replies fail the operation. No CLI fallback or external HTTP/provider call.
49|
50|The write envelope is `{id, method: "pane.report_metadata", params: {pane_id, source, seq, tokens, ttl_ms}}`, with the pinned environment pane ID, fixed source above, reserved numeric sequence, exactly the two input token keys, and `ttl_ms: 60000`. Serialize to UTF-8 JSON plus one newline; omit presentation/lifecycle fields. Readback uses `{id, method: "pane.get", params: {pane_id}}` with the same pinned ID. Require the matching string response ID, an object `result` and no `error`; pane readback additionally requires `result.type === "pane_info"`, the matching `result.pane.pane_id`, and its `tokens` map. A null patch succeeds only when that key is absent on readback. Never use a focused-pane default.
51|
52|Maintain one session generation and one serialized drain. Retain at most one latest pending snapshot; model events supersede older pending values. A callback from a retired generation cannot read context or initiate another request. Capture plain values before asynchronous work; never read an invalidated context.
53|
54|Keep a durable counter independent of Herdr's ephemeral tokens. Its prospective directory is `pi-model-logo-state` beside the global native `extensions` directory. Its filename is the lowercase SHA256 of UTF-8 `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH + U+0000 + HERDR_PANE_ID`, followed by `.json`; its sole content is `{"last":N}`. Require N to be a nonnegative JavaScript safe integer. Initial-install preflight provisions zero before activation only with release evidence that this source has never published for that socket/pane; token absence is not that evidence. Otherwise preserve the existing counter or stop. Runtime never initializes a missing counter. Cap reads at 64 bytes. Directory/file modes are 0700/0600, with current-user ownership and no symlink traversal. Corrupt, foreign-owned, symlinked, missing, unwritable or exhausted state stops publication with a generic warning; it is never silently reset. No session reference, title or transcript enters this store. Preflight forbids multiple producer processes for the same socket/pane. Within one process, serialize counter updates across reload generations using a process-scoped registry; retire old generation work before a new generation can publish. No lock file or wall-clock seed.
55|
56|For each update, including refresh and clearing:
57|
58|1. Read the owned counter, choose N = last + 1, and require N to be a safe integer. Persist `{"last":N}` to an exclusively created same-directory temporary file, sync and close it, then atomically rename it over the counter before any IPC write. Remove only this operation's own temporary file on failure. If persistence fails, send nothing. Read back the reserved counter before proceeding.
59|2. Report ID and reference together with source `user:radar-pi-model`, `seq: N` and `ttl_ms: 60000`. Clear both with null for shutdown or unavailable reference; clear ID alone for an unavailable model when the reference remains valid. Every attempt reserves a fresh number, including retries and cleanup.
60|3. Read back the pinned pane's inputs before acknowledging success; an API success may be an ignored old sequence. If a newer desired snapshot arrived, drain that snapshot next; do not resend the superseded one. Failure leaves only the latest desired snapshot pending for the next trigger.
61|
62|Persist-before-send allows skipped numbers after failure but prevents reuse after a process crash, reload, lease expiry, server restart between requests, or wall-clock change. Server token loss cannot erase the counter. Preserve counters during shutdown and rollback so same-pane reinstall remains safe; do not delete/reset them while the server can retain this source's sequence history. They are invisible feature-owned state, not sidebar tokens. Cleanup is allowed only after separately verifying that the pane lifetime has ended. Never allocate another sequence source to bypass a refusal. The reservation precedes the IPC request even if shutdown reaches its deadline; no unreserved clear may be sent.
63|
64|### Lifecycle, expiry and recovery
65|
66|The factory registers handlers only; it starts no sockets, processes or timers. `session_start` first retires old generation resources, then initializes eligible native TUI state, publishes fresh values and starts one unrefed 30000ms metadata-refresh timer. `model_select` publishes freshly read current values immediately; restoration uses `session_start`, not a presumed restore-sourced model event. Startup/reload/new/resume/fork all reinitialize from the supplied current context. Rename does not affect the model/reference or call a title API.
67|
68|The refresh is a metadata lease renewal, not terminal-title reconciliation: there are zero title writes. It republishes fresh values even if unchanged, so server token loss is recoverable without a prompt/restart. Recovery occurs on the next event or refresh after the same socket/pane becomes reachable and its authoritative Pi reference is available; no absolute wall-clock SLA under event-loop stalls is promised. If the reference is absent/mismatched, Radar remains blank until the existing integration establishes it. If the pane no longer exists, retire the publisher and its timer; never redirect to another pane. Changed socket/pane environment requires later separately authorized idle reload, not discovery or restart.
69|
70|On `session_shutdown`, retire generation/timer first, cancel outstanding sockets, discard old pending updates, and attempt the serialized null patch from captured data. Bound cleanup to 4000ms in total and destroy its sockets at that deadline. If clearing fails, the last successful ID/ref expires after its 60000ms lease; then Radar clears the model cells on its next successful frame. Leave Pi usable and the managed lifecycle integration untouched. Repeated shutdown is idempotent. Warn at most once per generation using generic text without identifiers, references, names, stack traces or payloads.
71|
72|Transient socket/server failure gets no tight retry loop: retain only the latest desired snapshot and retry on the next model/session trigger or scheduled refresh. Do not mark a failed or ignored write delivered. A valid empty agent list is not a failed list read: preserve Radar's existing failed-read semantics. No stale model cache or title/provider fallback is added.
73|
74|## 4. Pi-only consumer and family resolution
75|
76|In `lib/state.js`, carry the authoritative agent/session information and input tokens through the snapshot to row composition. For a resolved Pi entry, accept inputs only when the raw authoritative agent is `pi`, `agent_session.agent` is `pi`, session source is `herdr:pi`, kind is `path` or `id`, and the digest of its nonempty exact value equals `pi_model_ref`. Missing, expired, malformed or foreign data yields no model family. Do not mistake metadata `agent`/`applies_to_source` for token guards; enforcement is in this consumer.
77|
78|For Pi, never use terminal title, project/session names, provider or the old output token to find a model. Revalidate the input ID without repairing it. Select the final nonempty slash-delimited ID component; a trailing slash is unknown. Match case-insensitive ASCII aliases anchored at the identifier start. Alias boundary is end, digit, hyphen, dot or underscore; the reasoning alias `o[1-9]` allows end, hyphen, dot or underscore, not another digit. Exactly one family may match, otherwise return null.
79|
80|| Existing family key | Identifier-start aliases | Positive fixtures | Negative fixtures |
81||---|---|---|---|
82|| claude | claude, opus, sonnet, haiku, fable | claude-sonnet-4; anthropic/claude-opus-4 | my-claude; claudelike |
83|| gpt | gpt, codex; reasoning o[1-9] | gpt-5; codex-mini; o3; o1-preview | notgpt; project-o3; o10 |
84|| gemini | gemini | gemini-2.5-pro | mygemini |
85|| deepseek | deepseek | deepseek-r1 | notdeepseek |
86|| qwen | qwen | Qwen3-Coder-Next-80B-A3B; qwen-2.5 | qwenish; project-qwen |
87|| grok | grok | grok-4 | groklike |
88|| glm | glm | glm-4.5 | glmlike |

95|Each `test:` label is a required future automated implementation test, not a claim that it exists or has passed. Preserve these acceptance identities while testing the behavior specified here. 164|
165|Only model ID, reference digest, sequence counter and source/host/glyph identities enter feature metadata/evidence. Counter files contain only the last reserved integer. No session file content/path, prompt, transcript, credential, user title or task name is persisted; no payload controls are normalized into another model.

# Dispatching Reviewer Subagents

Use this whenever you spawn a CLI coding agent to produce an independent review of a spec, PR, or
code, especially when the review may come back needing revision.

## Confirm authorization before any dispatch

Dispatch only when the operator explicitly asks for a review or the specific task's approved workflow expressly requires one. An instruction to monitor CI, merge when green, clean up, or close a session is not review authorization; do not convert a prerequisite check into an unsolicited reviewer call. If a required independent verdict is missing, report that gate concisely and ask for the needed decision without starting a reviewer or making adjacent edits. A dispatched review is a separate action, not an automatic consequence of seeing a PR.

## Launch in the same turn you announce it

When the dispatch is authorized, build the packet and launch in that turn. Never reply "round N goes to …" and end the turn without a running process: the operator then asks for an ETA and finds nothing started. The first message after launch states the start time and the cap's end time, and nothing more.

## Dispatch one reviewer and keep its session

Treat a request for *a reviewer* as one reviewer and one model, even for high-risk work; do not add a second review from a default escalation policy when the operator specified the count or model. Before dispatch, pin the exact PR head/base and identify any in-scope uncommitted edits separately. If the verdict is incomplete or a factual claim needs correction, send a follow-up to the SAME CLI session with the exact missing paths/criteria; do not launch another reviewer or accept an informal verdict. Verify the process is actually stopped before saying it is stopped. Ensure the chosen CLI supports resume before launch.

When the operator explicitly asks for "another" or "a fresh" independent reviewer with "no biased info"/"no assumptions" after a prior round already found gaps, that IS a new, separately authorized dispatch (not the same-round follow-up rule above) — but the new subagent's context must contain ONLY the raw artifacts to inspect (PR numbers, repo paths, what claim is being verified), never the prior reviewer's findings, your own summary of them, or any framing of what was already fixed. State explicitly in its goal that it must search/read from scratch and form its own classification of each finding, not confirm or extend someone else's list. This is what makes the second opinion actually independent rather than an anchored rerun of the first.

## Default launcher: Hermes `delegate_task`

After explicit authorization to spawn the reviewer, use Hermes's built-in `delegate_task` by default, except when the operator requires incomplete work to return to the same agent/session: choose a resumable CLI before launch, because a completed delegate cannot satisfy that continuation requirement. Authorization for one reviewer does not authorize an extra orchestration, writing, investigation or amendment subagent; launch the requested reviewer directly unless additional delegation is explicitly approved. An explicitly named launcher still takes precedence. Before using an external CLI, check its login once and inspect its execution/resume help; then verify access through the actual reviewer session without starting a second reviewer. Operator shorthand "gpt-sol" means Codex `-m gpt-5.6-sol`. For Codex progress, parse its `--json` events for completed items rather than applying a Hermes transcript pattern. When a new round starts, stop the previous watcher so stale heartbeats do not masquerade as current activity. Steer messages to a running delegate arrive only after its current tool call ends; do not promise an instantaneous response.

## Select and verify the requested model

Pass the operator's explicit model ID to the CLI; it overrides default model pools and escalation. When only one reviewer is authorized, do not spawn a separate model for a smoke test: check the CLI's model selection syntax, launch the single reviewer, then verify its reported model in that session's structured result before accepting its review. A rejected model or silent substitution blocks the review; do not pick a replacement without direction.

When the operator reports an existing working login, compare the launcher's configuration, inherited endpoint and supported credential source with that working setup before requesting authentication again. Use the CLI's authorized credential-loading mechanism; never dump secrets or repair credential stores as part of a review dispatch. Confirm access through the actual reviewer session, not an authentication-status probe alone. A failed launch is not a review round: do not print placeholder severity counts or a findings table before a review actually returns. When diagnosing restricted Claude auth, report only helper presence, endpoint hostname and provider-variable presence; do not infer a suppressed helper when none exists. Compare a known successful launch's executable, host and shell initialization: a working remote claude.ai OAuth runtime can succeed with identical restricted/safe-mode flags while an unauthenticated local runtime cannot. If the operator authorizes transport recovery after zero inference, preserve the requested session UUID, model and read-only restrictions, transfer only the scoped source packet, and record source-path mappings and the explicit recovery deadline.

## Enforce read-only and protect secrets structurally

Constrain the CLI to Read/Glob/Grep and only the read-only Git/GitHub shell forms needed for the review; prose alone cannot prevent a Bash tool from reading credentials or changing state. Do not use a *plan* permission mode if the CLI treats it as an implementation-planning task and refuses a review; use a compatible read-only sandbox or narrow tool allowlist instead. Never grant broad shell access for production-config/variable commands, or ask the reviewer to dump environment JSON: these endpoints can print live secrets into the model transcript even when the intended field is only a branch. Supply a sanitized source-branch/deployment summary from the parent and label it parent-provided evidence. If a secret is exposed, stop further reads, never print its value while inspecting the transcript, alert the operator about rotation, and continue only within the same restricted session if the review remains authorized.

Before launch, map mandatory review steps to the restricted toolset. If the review skill requires current primary-source checks for external facts, allow public documentation fetches scoped to the needed domains (for Claude, `--tools Read,Glob,Grep,WebFetch` with `--allowedTools 'Read,Glob,Grep,WebFetch(domain:<official-domain>)'`). Keep production APIs, private data and unrelated network access excluded. Read-only must not mean denying the evidence access required for a valid verdict.

## Pack the evidence before launch

For manuscript work, complete the author's subtractive self-review before the next authorized independent review: remove repeated evidence, defensive review-response prose and unsupported implications; preserve sound passages, source qualifications and substantive disagreements. Then check each factual sentence against its source for actor, nested attribution, scope, action status and deadline semantics; check each inference for conditions the source does not establish. A clean voice check does not replace this evidence pass. Keep internal cutoff wording and publication-time rechecks in editorial notes; retain any date or qualification the reader needs to understand the claim. Measure before and after with the same counting method rather than comparing incompatible historical totals. Record this as author checking, never independent approval; exclude that record from the reviewer packet.

Before declaring any write, rewrite or amendment READY or done, personally walk the governing skill and every required linked file section by section against the actual artifact, source evidence and handoff. Build obligations from the operator's original messages; label assistant proposals, delegation instructions and reviewer recommendations separately, because none creates operator authority. Include the handoff rules themselves: status word, path, disposition counts and material limitations such as secondary-only citations, sources not re-retrieved, and amended text not yet reviewed. Treat a child's compliance checklist and a passing structural audit as claims to inspect, not proof of semantic compliance: hashes, counts and resolved labels cannot establish that a requirement was authorized or that its design is correct. Never make an audit assert a desired READY/BLOCKED label instead of deriving what its checks actually establish; report structural validity separately from the author's readiness verdict. When the operator asks "have you followed every rule?" and you have to answer no, the checklist was skipped. A skipped handoff rule is as much a violation as a skipped evidence rule. Write a verification line in an amendment record only after doing that check in the same pass: a whole-document reread means reading the file top to bottom, so diff-only checks and scripts don't count, and a false "reread" line is fabricated evidence. Test any replacement sentence against the finding's defect class before keeping it. When the surrounding text already answers the question, delete the unsupported claim rather than rewording it, because a reworded general claim usually repeats the same unsupported inference. Update the project's working notes (research context, evidence notes) in the same pass, as write-article's handoff requires.

When the operator says "same principles", carry forward the requested model, neutral-input rules, full-source coverage and time cap without asking them to restate these. Apply subsequent cap or monitoring corrections before launch: update both the brief and external watchdog, not just the acknowledgement. Package the current revision, not the previous review's snapshot, and do not carry forward its findings into a fresh unbiased review. When reusing a packet, replace the complete manuscript block, recompute manuscript and source-file hashes, and inspect retained context for embedded prior verdicts; changing only the launcher can silently review an obsolete revision.

A read-only sandbox usually has no network and no session history, so hand the reviewer a
parent-provided evidence directory instead of letting it guess: the operator's messages verbatim
(pulled from session history, tool output excluded — the reviewer must map obligations from the
source, not the spec's own ledger), raw read-only `gh` outputs the spec cites, and every external
primary source the spec cites, fetched today with an access timestamp. Gitleaks-scan the directory
before launch. If the spec's tables hold commands, state in the brief that `\|` in a table cell is
GFM's escaped pipe and must be read as `|` when running the command; otherwise the reviewer runs the
raw markdown, its regexes match nothing, and it files a false finding. When the operator answered decisions tersely ("I click", "it's ok", "approved"),
pack the assistant question each answer replied to, verbatim and labelled; user-only messages make
every such decision look unrecoverable and the reviewer will rightly raise a BLOCKER. For an unbiased manuscript review, supply the exact current body and references, the report outline and editorial guidelines, adjacent-section text, voice requirements and source material. Exclude author recommendation memos, self-assessment, evidence-status verdicts and prior findings from the neutral packet; these can anchor the reviewer even when embedded inside the draft file. Retain factual provenance and access limitations, including which supplied sources are excerpts rather than complete texts. Label adjacent prose as context, not an additional review target, and label provisional length budgets as provisional. Check the assigned article against available neighbouring material; do not turn missing contributions into a requirement to finish or wait for the whole report. Distinguish article-only typesetting from assembled-report pagination, and never derive a subsection minimum from a report-wide page budget. Record both the exact supplied body-and-references hash and the source-file hash when editorial notes are stripped; otherwise the review cannot be tied unambiguously to the supplied revision.

Brief template and launch commands: `references/reviewer-brief-and-launch.md`.

## Run in background; audit completeness before acceptance

Launch the one CLI session as a notified background process and capture its structured final result, model and session ID. After exit, independently compare the reviewer's per-path inventory with the live changed-file manifests, including deleted files and explicitly scoped local edits; enumerate every obligation, requirement, and acceptance criterion rather than trusting a declared total. A grep-only or unread file is not reviewed. If any path/pass is missing, resume the SAME session with the specific remainder and do not call its BLOCKED/APPROVED text a complete review. Recover the verdict from structured output; do not open raw CLI transcripts when they may contain secrets. Distinguish review completeness from approval, CI success, mergeability, and later deployment validation. When asked for review errors, lead with demonstrated code defects and their severity; separately name any unfinished review checks. If no defects were reported but mandatory coverage is missing, say both plainly: no reported defects, review unaccepted. Do not describe timeout, incomplete coverage, or failed launch as a code finding, and do not present a provisional PASS as accepted approval. Keep this status answer to the requested errors rather than replaying dispatch history. When asked whether a reviewed spec is ready to merge and hand off, check its working-tree state, branch, PR and required checks before answering. State any remaining commit/PR/check/merge steps explicitly: a PASS on an uncommitted worktree is review approval, not merge readiness. Treat that readiness question as advice, not authorization to commit, merge, close the session or dispatch implementation.

When the operator's instruction DOES authorize merging (e.g. "merge/ship"), before calling the merge: confirm the PR's `headRefOid` equals the SHA you just pushed (uncommitted amendments from a review round are easy to leave unpushed); check branch protection for required status-check contexts (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/<base>/protection`) and wait for that exact context to report success on the exact head SHA (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/status` or `check-runs`) rather than assuming a prior green run still applies; and clear any "DO NOT MERGE" marker left on the PR title from earlier WIP pushes. A merge rejected with "base branch policy prohibits the merge" means a required check hasn't reported yet on this SHA — wait for it, don't reach for `--admin`/`--auto` without the operator's say.

After merge, cleanup and record-keeping (deleting the merged branch/worktree, syncing other local clones, writing a session log) are not exempt from the same branch discipline just because they're "only a log file" or "only docs" — a repo's pre-commit hook can refuse any commit made directly on the primary checkout of the base branch, including a single-file doc/log add. Create a fresh worktree + branch for that commit too, push it, wait for the same required status check on its exact SHA, and merge it through the identical PR path rather than editing the base checkout in place.

**Hermes `delegate_task` subagents cannot be resumed once stopped or completed.** If the operator requires the same reviewer/session, do not substitute a new delegate for an incomplete one; select a resumable launcher upfront and retain its session ID. If continuation with a different delegate is authorized, limit its task to the missing coverage, retain the prior per-file record, and require a combined verdict with an independent spot-check of carried-forward evidence. Neither a timeout nor an incomplete result authorizes accepting the review or starting a new review round.

The "files the prior pass already cleared" claim you hand to the new subagent is that FIRST subagent's own self-report of what it did before being cut off — not an independently verified record, the same way any child's completion claim is unverified until checked. Tell the second subagent to independently re-verify at least one of the carried-forward claims (re-read one file, re-check one security-sensitive code path) rather than accepting the full prior-coverage claim on faith; report that spot-check explicitly in the combined verdict so the operator can see the resumed pass wasn't pure trust in an interrupted agent's unproven account of its own progress.

## Self-audits are not review rounds

Your own reread of a spec against its skill is author checking. Never number it as a review round,
and never let repeated self-audits stand in for the independent review the workflow expects. When
asked how many review rounds happened, count only actual reviewer dispatches that returned.

## Get fresh authorization for each round, don't self-trigger

A one-time instruction to dispatch a reviewer authorizes that ONE dispatch, not a standing policy to
redispatch after every subsequent fix/amendment round. Finishing a round of fixes is not itself a
signal to re-review — ask the operator before the next dispatch, even if an earlier round's verdict
was BLOCKED and you've since addressed every finding. Treat 'dispatch a reviewer' as scoped to the
instant it was said; carrying it forward as an implicit loop produces exactly the review-loop
frustration operators call out hardest. When in doubt, finish and report the fix round, then stop
and wait rather than dispatching again.

When the operator re-issues the exact same dispatch instruction verbatim (word-for-word, including a
repeated time cap), that IS fresh authorization for a new round — do not read a repeated instruction
as you having misread it the first time, and do not refuse or ask for clarification. Just dispatch
again. For an amended artifact or a requested fresh unbiased review, inspect the whole current revision without supplying prior findings. Carry forward coverage only for an explicitly authorized completion follow-up on an unchanged artifact, with independent spot-checks as described below.

A dispatch instruction's own completeness language ("a review that skips a pass is incomplete —
send it back", "don't accept it until every criterion is covered") authorizes sending an INCOMPLETE
review back to the same reviewer for more coverage. It does NOT authorize a brand-new round after a
COMPLETE review returns real findings and you fix them — that still needs a fresh ask. The two look
similar ("review wasn't good enough yet" vs. "review was fine, fixes landed, should we re-check")
but only the first is covered by the original instruction; conflating them is how one authorized
dispatch turns into an unauthorized loop of two or three.

## Re-review after amendment: dispatch fresh, not diff-only

When a spec/contract comes back from review with CHANGES REQUIRED and gets amended, the next round's
dispatch is a brand-new subagent, not a resume — and its instructions must say to review the WHOLE
current document independently, not just diff against the prior round's findings (this matches
skill-review-specs' own rule that a later review rechecks the entire contract, not only changed
lines). When the operator requests unbiased inputs, exclude prior findings and amendment claims;
the parent reconciles them against the fresh verdict afterward. Otherwise, any supplied finding
history must be treated as claims to re-verify, never as the author's proof of a completed fix. Also instruct it to
independently re-check any evidence-table citations, cross-reference collisions, or numbering/slot
claims (e.g. a phase or ID claimed to be "the first free one") against the real source, not against
what the spec or the prior review already asserted — an error that both the author and a first
reviewer missed will not be caught by a second reviewer who just trusts their agreement.

## Define convergence before round one

A review loop with no PASS threshold never converges: every fresh, blind reviewer adds new optional and unknown items, so CHANGES REQUIRED repeats indefinitely while the body grows. Put in the brief that PASS means zero demonstrated errors, unsupported inferences and material unknowns; minor unknowns are labelled, and taste never blocks. Require High/Medium/Low severity with optional taste never High. Because prior findings are excluded from the blind packet, the parent separately confirms each prior fix against the diff, so a later round cannot silently reopen settled wording. Track the blocking-finding count per round and follow principles-base §12 exactly: a second non-shrinking CHANGES REQUIRED, or the fourth one, means rewrite from facts instead of amending again. Raise that decision with the operator rather than requesting another round. An operator-ordered rewrite from facts restarts the round count for the new manuscript; record that in the amendment ledger. Amendments must not grow the body without operator approval. When a finding contradicts wording the governing skill's own examples give as correct, dispute it by quoting that example; when a finding is valid, fix every sentence with the same cause (for example, a sibling sentence drawing the same unsupported necessity), not only the quoted one.

When asked whether findings are valid, adjudicate each one against the actual text before answering: valid, partly valid (state the narrower true defect), or disputed (state the evidence). A reviewer can mislabel a deliberate operator constraint as a contradiction, or overstate a gap the next sentence already closes. A "rule X is missing from file Y" finding often means X exists under a label the reader did not recognise: grep Y for the rule's substance, dispute the finding with the quoted line, then reword the cross-reference so it names the rule by what it does ("stop amending when review.md calls for a rewrite"), because the next reader will make the same miss.

## Require explicit per-obligation/per-criterion coverage in the returned report

When dispatching a spec/contract reviewer, require the result to state coverage explicitly: every
obligation-ledger row and every acceptance criterion individually confirmed traceable/verifiable, or
flagged as a finding — a reviewer that reports "looks complete" without enumerating each one has not
demonstrated coverage. Require the exact verdict vocabulary the governing review skill defines (e.g.
PASS / CHANGES REQUIRED / UNVERIFIED) — an informal verdict ("looks good", "mostly fine") is an
incomplete review regardless of how much work was actually done, and must be sent back rather than
accepted.

Audit the limitations section against the governing checklist before accepting PASS: a missing mandatory primary-source check is unfinished work, not a harmless limitation merely because the reviewer found no contrary evidence. Restore narrowly scoped access and resume the same session for that specific gap; if required access remains unavailable, require the governing UNVERIFIED verdict rather than inventing a defect or accepting an unsupported PASS.

For Codex offline tests that need disposable files, a `read-only` sandbox can block all temporary-directory creation before assertions run. Preserve read-only source access by resuming the same session with an external artifact directory as `codex -C <artifact-dir> --sandbox workspace-write --add-dir <fixture-root> exec resume <session-id> ...`, never making the reviewed repository the writable working root. Use `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` and only the required fixture roots; inspect saved `turn_context` metadata to verify the actual model, cwd and sandbox policy, and verify no tracked source diff afterward. Keep the original wall-clock deadline across all resumes; do not reset it from a later `thread.started` event.

Verify received source coverage, not merely successful read commands: huge batched output and giant JSON lines can be truncated despite exit 0. Require bounded character pagination and receipt ranges for omitted content; decode embedded JSON before pagination. A complete, clearly delimited direct-input source packet is another way to avoid tool-output truncation, but the reviewer must acknowledge complete receipt and inspect it rather than inheriting the author's conclusions. Treat aggregate shell exit 0 as insufficient when earlier commands failed; capture each prerequisite's exit independently.

Before spending a completion follow-up's budget, reduce the task to the exact missing evidence and give the same reviewer complete readable source for those gaps. Challenge test-coverage claims by tracing which shipped branch each test reaches: successful dependency repair and pre-mutation refusal do not prove rollback after mutation. Require a genuinely different prior revision, a failure after checkout or dependency mutation, and assertions for restored revision, launcher and dependency state; removing the shipped restoration step must turn the regression red. If the reviewer retracts unsupported evidence, obtain a corrected formal verdict rather than accepting its earlier PASS.

For a completion follow-up on an unchanged artifact, retain the original per-item coverage and append the missing evidence; this remains the same round. Accept a multipart report only when the final verdict explicitly incorporates the earlier inspection and the combined artifacts retain every individual coverage row. Compare actual obligation/requirement/criterion/task ID sets with the returned rows, not just declared totals (a grouped row such as `OB-1–OB-15` is missing coverage, and an AC table that merges the brief's required columns into one is incomplete; check both with a parser, then send the report back), and recheck artifact/companion hashes before acceptance. Do not repeat completed passes merely to fill out an addendum.

Before launch, materialize the changed-file manifest separately for each pinned head/base pair in a multi-PR stack; retain target-qualified path IDs so the same path changed in two PRs receives two coverage entries. Give the reviewer every changed file, deleted files at the base, and the complete diff before it judges. Require substantive per-file reading evidence, explicit mandatory-pass coverage, individually sourced obligations/criteria, exact revisions and a formal verdict in the returned report. A JSON schema can enforce report shape, but neither schema validity nor a `complete` flag proves inspection: independently audit the evidence and actual ID sets before acceptance, and return omissions to the same session. A child’s compliance certificate is not evidence that every rule was followed; check temporal requirements such as pre-edit classification against the actual chronology rather than accepting later reconstruction as proof.

## Receiving findings is not authorization to amend

A reviewer's verdict (even CHANGES REQUIRED) is report material, not a trigger to act. Reviewing and
amending are two separately authorized actions in this workflow — do not chain straight from
"reviewer returned findings" into opening the amendment skill and patching the document, even if you
are confident of the fix. This bar applies equally to dispatching an AMENDMENT or fix subagent, not
just to patching the file yourself: spawning any subagent — reviewer or amender — is a distinct
authorized action, and a review dispatch's authorization does not carry forward to a follow-on
amendment dispatch. If the operator wants the fix made, they will say so as its own instruction;
until then, report the findings (or the requested table) and stop. If you did self-amend on an
explicit separate instruction, that instruction authorized YOU to amend, not a subagent to amend —
don't launch a delegate task for a step you were personally asked to do. Do exactly what the dispatch instruction named: if the operator capped the
output (e.g. "at the end, only print the table, nothing else"), stop there — present the findings (or
just the requested table) and wait. Only amend when the operator separately invokes that step (a
fresh "follow the amend-specs skill" instruction, or equivalent). Treat a narrowly-scoped verb
("dispatch a reviewer", "print the table") as capping the turn at that verb; it does not imply
follow-through into fixing what the review found, however obviously correct the fix would be.

## Severity tables: never invent a grade that was not returned

This is the single highest-frequency way this workflow angers the operator, so it gets its own
heading rather than staying buried in prose. This rule applies on ANY turn that produces a
findings/severity table, not only the turn where a reviewer was just dispatched — re-consult this
section every time the operator asks for counts, a table, or "the findings" from prior rounds,
even several turns later and even under repeated angry pressure to just produce numbers. The failure mode: several review rounds used
different, incompatible severity vocabularies (one round rated nothing, another used five
graduated levels, a third used a different five), the operator asks for "N findings per severity
(cols) per round, nothing else", and the instinct is to silently invent a mapping from each
round's actual labels onto the requested columns so every cell gets a number. That instinct is
fabrication, not formatting — and restating the same table request more forcefully (including with
anger) is a request for correct output, never authorization to start inventing data to satisfy it.

Require the governing review skill's exact severity vocabulary in the brief before dispatch (`skill-review-specs`: BLOCKER / MAJOR / MINOR; where no review skill defines one, High / Medium / Low). Prohibit hybrid grades and keep optional taste separate from defect severity. Validate the returned labels before counting. A request to change table columns is not authorization to regrade historical findings.

When table-only output is requested, return only the table: rounds as rows and that vocabulary's levels as columns; no descriptions, preamble or added total column unless requested. Parse each saved report's top-level finding IDs and explicit severity fields with a tool, then aggregate; do not dump entire reports or every stream event merely to count headings. Count each finding once, not sub-bullets or repeated coverage mentions. Never infer severity from priority order, mandatory/recommended/optional labels, wording or a CHANGES REQUIRED verdict. Never silently round a hybrid grade upward or classify an ungraded finding as Low. If historical reports cannot support the requested three-level breakdown, mark affected cells `Unknown` rather than zero or guessed counts; retain the original labels and reason in the audit artifact. Obtain an explicit mapping or authorization to reclassify before producing replacement numbers, and label any authorized reclassification as such rather than presenting it as the reviewer's original rating.

If the operator keeps re-demanding the same table after an `Unknown`-cell answer, the fix is to say
plainly which rounds have no compatible severity data and ask for the mapping decision — not to try
again with a guessed mapping on the theory that persistence implies permission. Silence or repeated
anger from the operator is not a mapping; it is pressure to still get this part right.

Table-only means zero words outside the table: no acceptance note, coverage remark or status line before or after it; record acceptance in the review artifacts instead. During the run, a heartbeat message is one short status sentence only. Run the heartbeat as one bounded background loop (`for i in 1 2 3; do sleep 180; hb.sh; pgrep -f <run> || break; done` with `heartbeat=180`), so it ends by itself when the reviewer exits. Kill a heartbeat watcher by its process tree (the background session), never only its `sleep`: killing `sleep` in `sleep N; hb.sh` still runs `hb.sh` and fires a stale notification. Answer a stale notification with nothing new, and never with a recap. When the reviewer exits before the watcher loop's next beat, stop the watcher's whole background session in the same turn you read the report; otherwise its remaining beats arrive after the table and each one draws a reply.

Keep coverage, limitations and verdicts in the review artifacts. Count actual review rounds, not failed launches or same-revision completion follow-ups. Record consumed process/session results; do not repeat the table when a delayed notification arrives for an already-reported result.

## Verify a post-review fix against raw bytes, not terminal display

After fixing a finding (e.g. a reviewer flagged a credential-shaped placeholder like `Bearer ***`
in a doc's health-check command), re-verifying the fix with `search_files`/`read_file`/terminal
`cat`/`grep` on that line can keep showing the masked `***` even after the real file content is
already correct — terminal and file-reading tool output redact anything matching a
`Bearer <token>`-shaped pattern as a safety measure, independent of what is actually on disk.
Don't conclude the edit failed and re-patch or re-write the file from a masked display; confirm
with a raw byte-level read (e.g. Python `open(path, "rb").read()` and check byte counts / hex for
the literal string) before repeating an edit that may have already landed. Also check `git
status`/`git diff` for "nothing to commit" as a faster signal that the working tree already
matches what you intended.

## Reviewing self-authored documentation/guides

When the reviewer's target is a guide/doc you wrote yourself (not a spec or code diff), its job is
factual accuracy, not prose quality. Instruct it to: (1) verify every concrete claim — file paths,
function/endpoint names, env var names, cron/workflow names — against the actual current source,
not the doc's own prose; (2) actually RUN every command the doc tells a reader to run (health
checks, setup steps) and report the real exit code/output, flagging any command that doesn't
produce what the doc claims; (3) check structural requirements (required headings, counts) exactly.
Self-authored docs reliably contain at least one command that was never actually executed (a typo'd
variable, a wrong relative path, a stale claim) — this is a high-yield review type for catching
real, reproducible bugs cheaply, worth dispatching even when the operator only asked for a general
review pass over new documentation.

## Full-text evidence reviews

A `search-only backend cannot extract URL content` error is a routing failure, not proof the source is inaccessible. A bounded fallback, after checking the installed implementation, is a process-local override of `tools.web_tools._get_extract_backend` to `firecrawl` while calling `web_extract_tool` under Hermes's own venv. # Codex CLI

Delegate coding tasks to [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) via the Hermes terminal. Codex is OpenAI's autonomous coding agent CLI.

## When to use

- Building features
- Refactoring
- PR reviews
- Batch issue fixing

Requires the codex CLI and a git repository.

## Prerequisites

- Codex installed: `npm install -g @openai/codex`
- OpenAI auth configured: either `OPENAI_API_KEY` or Codex OAuth credentials
  from the Codex CLI login flow
- **Must run inside a git repository** — Codex refuses to run outside one
- Use `pty=true` in terminal calls — Codex is an interactive terminal app

For Hermes itself, `model.provider: openai-codex` uses Hermes-managed Codex
OAuth from `~/.hermes/auth.json` after `hermes auth add openai-codex`. For the
standalone Codex CLI, a valid CLI OAuth session may live under
`~/.codex/auth.json`; do not treat a missing `OPENAI_API_KEY` alone as proof
that Codex auth is missing.

## One-Shot Tasks

```
terminal(command="codex exec 'Add dark mode toggle to settings'", workdir="~/project", pty=true)
```

For scratch work (Codex needs a git repo):
```
terminal(command="cd $(mktemp -d) && git init && codex exec 'Build a snake game in Python'", pty=true)
```

## Background Mode (Long Tasks)

```
# Start in background with PTY
terminal(command="codex exec --sandbox workspace-write 'Refactor the auth module'", workdir="~/project", background=true, pty=true)
# Returns session_id

# Monitor progress
process(action="poll", session_id="<id>")
process(action="log", session_id="<id>")

# Send input if Codex asks a question
process(action="submit", session_id="<id>", data="yes")

# Kill if needed
process(action="kill", session_id="<id>")
```

## Key Flags

| Flag | Effect |
|------|--------|
| `exec "prompt"` | One-shot execution, exits when done |
| `--sandbox workspace-write` (`-s`) | Sandboxed but auto-approves file changes in the workspace (the recommended auto-build mode) |
| `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` | No sandbox, no approvals (fastest, most dangerous; `--yolo` still works as a hidden alias) |
| `--sandbox danger-full-access` | No Codex sandbox; useful when the host service context breaks bubblewrap |

> **Deprecated:** `--full-auto` still works but the live CLI warns to use `--sandbox workspace-write` instead.

## Hermes Gateway Caveat

When invoking the Codex CLI from a Hermes gateway/service context (for example,
Telegram-driven agent sessions), Codex `workspace-write` sandboxing may fail even
when the same command works in the user's interactive shell. A typical symptom is
bubblewrap/user-namespace errors such as `setting up uid map: Permission denied`
or `loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted`.

In that context, prefer:

```
codex exec --sandbox danger-full-access "<task>"
```

Use process boundaries as the safety layer instead: explicit `workdir`, clean git
status before launch, narrow task prompts, `git diff` review, targeted tests, and
human/agent confirmation before committing broad changes.

## PR Reviews

Clone to a temp directory for safe review:

```
terminal(command="REVIEW=$(mktemp -d) && git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git $REVIEW && cd $REVIEW && gh pr checkout 42 && codex review --base origin/main", pty=true)
```

## Parallel Issue Fixing with Worktrees

```
# Create worktrees
terminal(command="git worktree add -b fix/issue-78 ~/.hermes/cache/scratch/issue-78 main", workdir="~/project")
terminal(command="git worktree add -b fix/issue-99 ~/.hermes/cache/scratch/issue-99 main", workdir="~/project")

# Launch Codex in each
terminal(command="codex --sandbox workspace-write exec 'Fix issue #78: <description>. Commit when done.'", workdir="~/.hermes/cache/scratch/issue-78", background=true, pty=true)
terminal(command="codex --sandbox workspace-write exec 'Fix issue #99: <description>. Commit when done.'", workdir="~/.hermes/cache/scratch/issue-99", background=true, pty=true)

# Monitor
process(action="list")

# After completion, push and create PRs
terminal(command="cd ~/.hermes/cache/scratch/issue-78 && git push -u origin fix/issue-78")
terminal(command="gh pr create --repo user/repo --head fix/issue-78 --title 'fix: ...' --body '...'")

# Cleanup
terminal(command="git worktree remove ~/.hermes/cache/scratch/issue-78", workdir="~/project")
```

## Batch PR Reviews

```
# Fetch all PR refs
terminal(command="git fetch origin '+refs/pull/*/head:refs/remotes/origin/pr/*'", workdir="~/project")

# Review multiple PRs in parallel
terminal(command="codex exec 'Review PR #86. git diff origin/main...origin/pr/86'", workdir="~/project", background=true, pty=true)
terminal(command="codex exec 'Review PR #87. git diff origin/main...origin/pr/87'", workdir="~/project", background=true, pty=true)

# Post results
terminal(command="gh pr comment 86 --body '<review>'", workdir="~/project")
```

## Rules

1. **Always use `pty=true`** — Codex is an interactive terminal app and hangs without a PTY
2. **Git repo required** — Codex won't run outside a git directory. Use `mktemp -d && git init` for scratch
3. **Use `exec` for one-shots** — `codex exec "prompt"` runs and exits cleanly
4. **`--sandbox workspace-write` for building** — auto-approves changes within the sandbox (`--full-auto` is deprecated for this)
5. **Background for long tasks** — use `background=true` and monitor with `process` tool
6. **Don't interfere** — monitor with `poll`/`log`, be patient with long-running tasks
7. **Parallel is fine** — run multiple Codex processes at once for batch work

3|These are synthetic review cases, not claims about a live repository. Read with `../skill-review-specs.md`; replace illustrative paths with actual sources before issuing a real finding.
4|
5|## Happy path: reject a false positive

10|
11|## Guarded variant: an unsafe export
12|
13|**Mandate:** Export account data. The draft says “authenticated users may export their accounts,” but an acceptance check only asserts HTTP 200 for the owner. The codebase has a tenant-scoped read path, yet the proposed export query does not name tenant filtering, prohibited data classes, failure logging, or expiry. The operator has not decided whether admins may export other users' records.
14|
15|Return `CHANGES REQUIRED`. Finding: `BLOCKER · export authorization/acceptance row · owner-only happy-path test cannot reject cross-tenant data exposure · test another tenant's account and prove exclusion; do not infer admin policy`. Cite the actual mandate, data model, and test at inspected revisions. Flag the missing operator decision separately; do not decide it, run an export, or rewrite the spec. If data access is unavailable, keep the confirmed contract finding but mark the actual data-exposure claim **unverified**, not a confirmed leak.
16|
17|## Anti-pattern and correction: a plausible but unproven objection
18|
19|**Draft:** “After receiving a job, retry once; on the second failure send it to the dead-letter queue.” **Reviewer claim:** “This must retry five times; industry best practice.” No higher-level policy, product decision or measured failure supports five retries. Discard the objection. If the existing queue config actually retries three times *before* the consumer sees the failure, cite the config and flag the real ambiguity: an implementer could enqueue a message six times while believing the contract allows two attempts. Minimal correction: define whether the retry count is end-to-end or consumer-local, grounded in the operator's desired failure policy. This is a contract finding, not a mandate to use a particular implementation.
20|
21|## Limit case: inaccessible source
22|
23|A spec asserts that an external API supports atomic bulk upsert, but the reviewer cannot reach the provider documentation and no verified contract test is available. Do not report “the API lacks atomic upsert” or PASS. Return `UNVERIFIED · provider contract unavailable · need the current official API documentation or a safe contract probe`. A 403 or timeout is an access failure, not evidence of missing functionality.
