# GitHub Pull Request Workflow

Complete guide for managing the PR lifecycle. Each section shows the `gh` way first, then the `git` + `curl` fallback for machines without `gh`.

## Prerequisites

- Authenticated with GitHub (see `github-auth` skill)
- Inside a git repository with a GitHub remote

### Quick Auth Detection

```bash
# Determine which method to use throughout this workflow
if command -v gh &>/dev/null && gh auth status &>/dev/null; then
  AUTH="gh"
else
  AUTH="git"
  # Ensure we have a token for API calls
  if [ -z "$GITHUB_TOKEN" ]; then
    if _hermes_env="${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/.env"; [ -f "$_hermes_env" ] && grep -q "^GITHUB_TOKEN=" "$_hermes_env"; then
      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(grep "^GITHUB_TOKEN=" "$_hermes_env" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2 | tr -d '\n\r')
    elif grep -q "github.com" ~/.git-credentials 2>/dev/null; then
      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(uv run python "${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/github/github-auth/scripts/git-credential-token.py")
    fi
  fi
fi
echo "Using: $AUTH"
```

### Extracting Owner/Repo from the Git Remote

Many `curl` commands need `owner/repo`. Extract it from the git remote:

```bash
# Works for both HTTPS and SSH remote URLs
REMOTE_URL=$(git remote get-url origin)
OWNER_REPO=$(echo "$REMOTE_URL" | sed -E 's|.*github\.com[:/]||; s|\.git$||')
OWNER=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f1)
REPO=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f2)
echo "Owner: $OWNER, Repo: $REPO"
```

---

## 1. Branch Creation

This part is pure `git` — identical either way:

```bash
# Make sure you're up to date
git fetch origin
git checkout main && git pull origin main

# Create and switch to a new branch
git checkout -b feat/add-user-authentication
```

Branch naming conventions:
- `feat/description` — new features
- `fix/description` — bug fixes
- `refactor/description` — code restructuring
- `docs/description` — documentation
- `ci/description` — CI/CD changes

## 2. Making Commits

Use the agent's file tools (`write_file`, `patch`) to make changes, then commit:

```bash
# Stage specific files
git add src/auth.py src/models/user.py tests/test_auth.py

# Commit with a conventional commit message
git commit -m "feat: add JWT-based user authentication

- Add login/register endpoints
- Add User model with password hashing
- Add auth middleware for protected routes
- Add unit tests for auth flow"
```

Commit message format (Conventional Commits):
```
type(scope): short description

Longer explanation if needed. Wrap at 72 characters.
```

Types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `ci`, `chore`, `perf`

## 3. Pushing and Creating a PR

### Push the Branch (same either way)

```bash
git push -u origin HEAD
```

### Create the PR

**With gh:**

```bash
gh pr create \
  --title "feat: add JWT-based user authentication" \
  --body "## Summary
- Adds login and register API endpoints
- JWT token generation and validation

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit tests pass

Closes #42"
```

Options: `--draft`, `--reviewer user1,user2`, `--label "enhancement"`, `--base develop`

**With git + curl:**

```bash
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)

curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.v3+json" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls \
  -d "{
    \"title\": \"feat: add JWT-based user authentication\",
    \"body\": \"## Summary\nAdds login and register API endpoints.\n\nCloses #42\",
    \"head\": \"$BRANCH\",
    \"base\": \"main\"
  }"
```

The response JSON includes the PR `number` — save it for later commands.

To create as a draft, add `"draft": true` to the JSON body.

## 4. Monitoring CI Status

### Check CI Status

**With gh:**

```bash
# One-shot check
gh pr checks

# Watch until all checks finish (polls every 10s)
gh pr checks --watch
```

**With git + curl:**

```bash
# Get the latest commit SHA on the current branch
SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

# Query the combined status
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/commits/$SHA/status \
  | python -c "
import sys, json
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
print(f\"Overall: {data['state']}\")
for s in data.get('statuses', []):
    print(f\"  {s['context']}: {s['state']} - {s.get('description', '')}\")"

# Also check GitHub Actions check runs (separate endpoint)
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/commits/$SHA/check-runs \
  | python -c "
import sys, json
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
for cr in data.get('check_runs', []):
    print(f\"  {cr['name']}: {cr['status']} / {cr['conclusion'] or 'pending'}\")"
```

### Poll Until Complete (git + curl)

```bash
# Simple polling loop — check every 30 seconds, up to 10 minutes
SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  STATUS=$(curl -s \
    -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
    https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/commits/$SHA/status \
    | python -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['state'])")
  echo "Check $i: $STATUS"
  if [ "$STATUS" = "success" ] || [ "$STATUS" = "failure" ] || [ "$STATUS" = "error" ]; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 30
done
```

## 5. Auto-Fixing CI Failures

When CI fails, diagnose and fix. This loop works with either auth method.

### Step 1: Get Failure Details

**With gh:**

```bash
# List recent workflow runs on this branch
gh run list --branch $(git branch --show-current) --limit 5

# View failed logs
gh run view <RUN_ID> --log-failed
```

**With git + curl:**

```bash
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)

# List workflow runs on this branch
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs?branch=$BRANCH&per_page=5" \
  | python -c "
import sys, json
runs = json.load(sys.stdin)['workflow_runs']
for r in runs:
    print(f\"Run {r['id']}: {r['name']} - {r['conclusion'] or r['status']}\")"

# Get failed job logs (download as zip, extract, read)
RUN_ID=<run_id>
curl -s -L \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/logs \
  -o /tmp/ci-logs.zip
cd /tmp && unzip -o ci-logs.zip -d ci-logs && cat ci-logs/*.txt
```

### Step 2: Fix and Push

After identifying the issue, use file tools (`patch`, `write_file`) to fix it:

```bash
git add <fixed_files>
git commit -m "fix: resolve CI failure in <check_name>"
git push
```

### Step 3: Verify

Re-check CI status using the commands from Section 4 above.

### Auto-Fix Loop Pattern

When asked to auto-fix CI, follow this loop:

1. Check CI status → identify failures
2. Read failure logs → understand the error
3. Use `read_file` + `patch`/`write_file` → fix the code
4. `git add . && git commit -m "fix: ..." && git push`
5. Wait for CI → re-check status
6. Repeat if still failing (up to 3 attempts, then ask the user)

## 6. Merging

**With gh:**

```bash
# Squash merge + delete branch (cleanest for feature branches)
gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch

# Enable auto-merge (merges when all checks pass)
gh pr merge --auto --squash --delete-branch
```

**With git + curl:**

```bash
PR_NUMBER=<number>

# Merge the PR via API (squash)
curl -s -X PUT \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/merge \
  -d "{
    \"merge_method\": \"squash\",
    \"commit_title\": \"feat: add user authentication (#$PR_NUMBER)\"
  }"

# Delete the remote branch after merge
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
git push origin --delete $BRANCH

# Switch back to main locally
git checkout main && git pull origin main
git branch -d $BRANCH
```

Merge methods: `"merge"` (merge commit), `"squash"`, `"rebase"`

### Enable Auto-Merge (curl)

```bash
# Auto-merge requires the repo to have it enabled in settings.
# This uses the GraphQL API since REST doesn't support auto-merge.
PR_NODE_ID=$(curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER \
  | python -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['node_id'])")

curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/graphql \
  -d "{\"query\": \"mutation { enablePullRequestAutoMerge(input: {pullRequestId: \\\"$PR_NODE_ID\\\", mergeMethod: SQUASH}) { clientMutationId } }\"}"
```

## 7. Complete Workflow Example

```bash
# 1. Start from clean main
git checkout main && git pull origin main

# 2. Branch
git checkout -b fix/login-redirect-bug

# 3. (Agent makes code changes with file tools)

# 4. Commit
git add src/auth/login.py tests/test_login.py
git commit -m "fix: correct redirect URL after login

Preserves the ?next= parameter instead of always redirecting to /dashboard."

# 5. Push
git push -u origin HEAD

# 6. Create PR (picks gh or curl based on what's available)
# ... (see Section 3)

# 7. Monitor CI (see Section 4)

# 8. Merge when green (see Section 6)
```

## Useful PR Commands Reference

| Action | gh | git + curl |
|--------|-----|-----------|
| List my PRs | `gh pr list --author @me` | `curl -s -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls?state=open"` |

| Close PR | `gh pr close N` | `curl -X PATCH .../pulls/N -d '{"state":"closed"}'` |
| Check out someone's PR | `gh pr checkout N` | `git fetch origin pull/N/head:pr-N && git checkout pr-N` |

{"content": "1|---
2|name: skill-git-multi-agent
3|description: Single source of truth for Git across parallel-agent projects: worktree lifecycle, branch flow, rebase, CI monitoring, and setup.
4|source: canon
5|canon_version: HEAD
6|---
7|
8|# Skill: Git Workflow: Multi-Agent
9|
10|Single source of truth for Git workflow across all parallel-agent projects. Worktree lifecycle, branch flow, rebase, CI monitoring, and one-time portable-worktree setup. `skill-branching-strategy.md` remains canonical for its §Cross-Repo Ordering content; `skill-worktree-workflow.md` is fully superseded and now a stub.
11|
12|---
13|
14|## Invariants (never violated)
15|
16|1. **Main checkout always on the integration branch, before, during, and after every session.** Never a feature branch, never the deploy branch. Read-only: no edits, no commits, no staged files. Leave it on the integration branch when done.
17|2. **Every agent works in a worktree.** No exceptions, even for one-line changes.
18|3. **One worktree per branch.** Two agents never share a worktree.
19|4. **Every branch references a Linear ID.** Block work also references its phase and block ID.
20|5. **All PRs target the integration branch.** Only `hotfix/*` may bypass.
21|6. **Always rebase on the integration branch before pushing.** No exceptions, skipping causes out-of-date rejections and integration conflicts.
22|7. **Monitor CI after every push. Do not proceed until all checks are green.** Fix failures before any next step.
23|
24|---
25|
26|## One-time repo setup
27|
28|Required before adding any worktree. Apply once per clone (new or existing). Implements `principles-base.md §14 Portability, Relative-path worktrees`. Requires Git ≥ 2.48 on every machine that will touch the repo.
29|
30|Because `.git/config` is never tracked, this setup cannot be encoded as a tracked git artifact. The portable solution is a **tracked bootstrap script** copied from the kit's `templates/meta/scripts/setup-repo.sh` into each repo's `scripts/setup-repo.sh`, then wired into the package manager's install lifecycle so contributors don't have to remember to run it.
31|
32|### Canonical script
33|
34|The kit template at `templates/meta/scripts/setup-repo.sh` does the full sequence idempotently:
35|
36|```
37|git config core.repositoryformatversion 1   # only if currently 0
38|git config worktree.useRelativePaths true   # implicitly enables extensions.relativeWorktrees
39|git worktree repair                          # converts pre-existing worktrees; no-op otherwise
40|```
41|
42|It also guards on Git version (≥ 2.48), resolves to the repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, exits silently when not in a git context (so it can't break tarball installs), and prints a one-line confirmation. Copy the script body into the project unchanged, do not symlink across repos (defeats portability). The leading comment block and the final echo message may be project-localized; the executable body must remain functionally identical so any future fix to the canonical can be re-applied with `diff` confidence.
43|
44|### Wiring variants
45|
46|Pick the variant that matches the repo's package manager. The script must auto-run after a fresh clone for the rule to hold across machines.
47|
48|| Repo type | Wiring | Trigger |
49||:--|:--|:--|
50|| Node (npm / pnpm / yarn) | Add `"prepare": "./scripts/setup-repo.sh"` (or `"../scripts/setup-repo.sh"` if `package.json` is in a subdirectory) to the install-time package's `package.json`. | `npm install` / `pnpm install` |
51|| Python (poetry) | Add a `tool.poetry.scripts` entry or a `poetry run` invocation in the project's bootstrap doc; or use a `Makefile setup` target. | `poetry install` or `make setup` |
52|| Plain (no package manager) | Document `./scripts/setup-repo.sh` as the first step in the README "Setup" section. | Manual, once per clone |
53|| Multi-repo workspace (e.g. `lens-app/` + `lens-meta/`) | Each repo carries its own `scripts/setup-repo.sh`. The workspace-root `README.md` / `AGENTS.md` lists both. | One per repo |
54|
55|### Migration order matters
56|
57|If you ever apply the raw commands by hand (e.g. on a repo that can't run shell scripts), bump `core.repositoryformatversion` to `1` *before* enabling the extension or `useRelativePaths`. Setting the extension on a version-0 repo leaves Git unable to operate on it until the version is bumped.
58|
59|---
60|
61|## Setup (once per session)
62|
63|```
64|cd {main-checkout}
65|git checkout {integration-branch}        # verify — fix if wrong
66|git fetch --prune origin                 # prunes remote-tracking refs for deleted branches
67|git branch -vv                           # [gone] = orphaned; note it — do NOT remove here (TRON-FLYNN GC owns it)
68|git worktree list                        # inspect (read-only) — situational awareness, not cleanup
69|gh pr list --base {integration-branch} --state open   # conflict check
70|```
71|
72|Session start is **read-only**: verify your checkout, inspect, and run the conflict check, do not remove other worktrees/branches here (see §Worktree teardown & orphan GC). If any open PR touches your task's files → **stop, report to user**.
73|
74|---
75|
76|## Branch naming
77|
78|| Work type | Pattern | Example |
79||:--|:--|:--|
80|| Block work | `{type}/B{PP}-{BB}-L{NNN}-{slug}` | `feat/B06-13-L123-github-actions-ci` |
81|| Non-block work | `{type}/adhoc-L{NNN}-{slug}` | `fix/adhoc-L456-typo-in-faq` |
82|| Hotfix | `hotfix/B{PP}-{BB}-L{NNN}-{slug}` or `hotfix/adhoc-L{NNN}-{slug}` | `hotfix/adhoc-L789-broken-login-redirect` |
83|
84|Rules: type and slug lowercase · `B` and `L` uppercase · phase and block numbers each have at least two digits · Linear ID required on every branch · every task inside a block keeps its `B{PP}-{BB}` · `hotfix/` is the only type that may PR into the deploy branch.
85|
86|---
87|
88|## Worktree lifecycle
89|
90|### Path conventions
91|
92|Canonical: `principles-base.md §14 Worktree path`. Not project-overridable.
93|
94|| Repo class | Path | Example |
95||:--|:--|:--|
96|| Multi-repo project (canon-extended, app, meta, …) | `{project}/worktrees/{repo}--{branch}/` | `hiresling.ai/worktrees/hiresling-app--feat-B90-01-L123-drafts/` |
97|| Single-repo / canon (e.g. `tortuga/`) | `{repo}/.worktrees/{branch}/` (gitignored) | `tortuga/.worktrees/chore/adhoc-L456-agent-system/` |
98|
99|The code blocks below show the multi-repo flow as default. For single-repo / canon, substitute `../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}` with `.worktrees/{branch}` and `cd {main-checkout}` with `cd {repo}` (the main checkout *is* the repo root). Parent dirs (`worktrees/` or `.worktrees/{nested}/`) must exist before `git worktree add`, `mkdir -p` first if needed.
100|
101|### Create (new branch)
102|
103|```
104|cd {main-checkout}
105|git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} -b {branch} origin/{integration-branch}
106|cd ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
107|```
108|
109|### Resume (existing branch with open PR)
110|
111|If the branch exists locally:
112|
113|```
114|cd {main-checkout}
115|git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} {branch}
116|cd ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
117|git pull --ff-only origin {branch}
118|```
119|
120|If the branch only exists on origin (no local ref yet):
121|
122|```
123|cd {main-checkout}
124|git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} -b {branch} origin/{branch}
125|cd ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
126|```
127|
128|### Work
129|
130|All reads, edits, commits, and pushes happen **inside the worktree**. Never in the main checkout.
131|
132|Commit at each task boundary, not at session end.
133|
134|```
135|git add {files}
136|git commit -m "{type}({scope}): {description}"   # Conventional Commits
137|```
138|
139|### Push
140|
141|First push:
142|
143|```
144|git fetch origin
145|git rebase origin/{integration-branch}
146|git push -u origin {branch}
147|```
148|
149|Re-push after rebase or amend:
150|
151|```
152|git fetch origin
153|git rebase origin/{integration-branch}
154|git push --force-with-lease origin {branch}
155|```
156|
157|Rebase conflict during push:
158|
159|```
160|# resolve conflict in file(s)
161|git add {resolved-files}
162|git rebase --continue
163|git push --force-with-lease origin {branch}
164|```
165|
166|### Monitor CI
167|
168|```
169|gh pr checks {PR-number} --watch
170|```
171|
172|Do not open a PR, request review, or proceed to the next task until all checks pass. If any check fails → fix, commit, push, rebase, repeat.
173|
174|### Open PR
175|
176|```
177|gh pr create --base {integration-branch} --title "{commit subject}" --body "Block: {block-id}"
178|```
179|
180|### Cleanup (after PR merges)
181|
182|Confirm the PR is merged before running:
183|
184|```
185|gh pr view {PR-number} --json state --jq '.state'   # must return MERGED
186|cd {main-checkout}
187|git fetch --prune origin
188|git worktree remove ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
189|git branch -D {branch}
190|git pull --ff-only origin {integration-branch}
191|```
192|
193|---
194|
195|## Meta repos (`.repo-class=meta`)
196|
197|Meta repos (project knowledge bases, agent docs, logs, blocks) drop **only** the PR/staging ceremony, the worktree-mandatory rule still applies.
198|
199|Flow:
200|
201|```
202|cd {main-checkout}                                # meta repo root
203|git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} -b {branch} origin/main
204|cd ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
205|# work + commit
206|git fetch origin
207|git rebase origin/main
208|git push origin {branch}:main                     # direct push to main
209|cd {main-checkout}
210|git worktree remove ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
211|git branch -D {branch}
212|git pull --ff-only origin main
213|```
214|
215|`.githooks/pre-push` template allows this when `.repo-class=meta`; for canon and app it enforces the PR flow.
216|
217|---
218|
219|## Hook enforcement
220|
221|A `.githooks/pre-commit` hook (kit template: `templates/meta/.githooks/pre-commit`, installed by `scripts/setup-repo.sh`) blocks any commit that did not originate from an added worktree. Applies to every `.repo-class` value (canon, meta, app). Detection: `git rev-parse --git-dir` lacking `.git/worktrees/` substring → fail.
222|
223|Hook failure message:
224|
225|```
226|✘ pre-commit blocked — commit must run in an added worktree, not the main checkout.
227|  Single-repo / canon:  git worktree add .worktrees/{branch} -b {branch} origin/main
228|  Multi-repo project:   git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} -b {branch} origin/{integration-branch}
229|```
230|
231|Bypassing with `--no-verify` violates Invariant 1 and `principles-base.md §14`.
232|
233|---
234|
235|## Hook integration patterns
236|
237|`.githooks/` is a **library of canon-prescribed scripts**, `pre-commit` and `pre-push` MUST fire on their respective events, but the dispatcher is the repo's choice. `scripts/setup-repo.sh` detects an existing dispatcher (`lefthook.yml`, `.husky/`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) and skips the `core.hooksPath=.githooks` override (which would silently suppress the dispatcher's own `.git/hooks/` installation).
238|
239|Pick the pattern that matches your repo.
240|
241|### Pattern A: git native (default, no dispatcher)
242|
243|No `lefthook.yml` / `.husky/` / `.pre-commit-config.yaml` at repo root. `scripts/setup-repo.sh` sets `core.hooksPath=.githooks` and git invokes the canon scripts directly. Nothing else to wire.
244|
245|### Pattern B: lefthook
246|
247|Add to `lefthook.yml`:
248|
249|```yaml
250|pre-commit:
251|  commands:
252|    canon-pre-commit:
253|      run: bash .githooks/pre-commit
254|      fail_text: "Canon pre-commit failed (see principles-base.md §14)"
255|
256|pre-push:
257|  commands:
258|    canon-pre-push:
259|      run: bash .githooks/pre-push "$1" "$2"
260|      fail_text: "Canon pre-push failed (see principles-base.md §14)"
261|```
262|
263|**⚠ Re-install warning.** `lefthook install` writes dispatcher scripts into `.git/hooks/` and may also touch `core.hooksPath` depending on the lefthook version. After any `lefthook install`, run `scripts/setup-repo.sh` again so its dispatcher detection unsets a stale `core.hooksPath=.githooks` if one snuck back in. Order: `lefthook install` first, `setup-repo.sh` second.
264|
265|### Pattern C: husky
266|
267|`.husky/pre-commit`:
268|
269|```sh
270|#!/usr/bin/env sh
271|. "$(dirname -- "$0")/_/husky.sh"
272|bash .githooks/pre-commit
273|```
274|
275|`.husky/pre-push`:
276|
277|```sh
278|#!/usr/bin/env sh
279|. "$(dirname -- "$0")/_/husky.sh"
280|bash .githooks/pre-push "$@"
281|```
282|
283|`chmod +x .husky/pre-commit .husky/pre-push`. Husky installs into `.git/hooks/` on `husky install`; `setup-repo.sh` leaves `core.hooksPath` unset when `.husky/` is detected so husky's installation is not suppressed.
284|
285|### Pattern D: pre-commit-framework
286|
287|Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:
288|
289|```yaml
290|repos:
291|  - repo: local
292|    hooks:
293|      - id: canon-pre-commit
294|        name: Canon pre-commit (worktree + integration-branch guard)
295|        entry: bash .githooks/pre-commit
296|        language: system
297|        stages: [pre-commit]
298|        pass_filenames: false
299|      - id: canon-pre-push
300|        name: Canon pre-push (reachability check)
301|        entry: bash .githooks/pre-push
302|        language: system
303|        stages: [pre-push]
304|        pass_filenames: false
305|```
306|
307|Run `pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push` after editing. Same caveat as lefthook: after any re-install, re-run `scripts/setup-repo.sh`.
308|
309|### Verifying wire-up
310|
311|After any wire-up change, validate from the main checkout AND from an added worktree:
312|
313|```sh
314|# In main checkout — pre-commit must FAIL:
315|git commit --allow-empty -m "verify: should-fail"
316|
317|# In a worktree off the integration branch — pre-commit must PASS:
318|git worktree add .worktrees/verify -b chore/adhoc-L123-verify-wireup origin/main  # or origin/staging for apps
319|cd .worktrees/verify && git commit --allow-empty -m "verify: should-pass"
320|```
321|
322|If both behave correctly, the canon scripts are firing through the chosen dispatcher.
323|
324|---
325|
326|## Worktree teardown & orphan GC
327|
328|Three distinct responsibilities, do not conflate them:
329|
330|- **Session start, read-only.** Inspect (`git branch -vv`, `git worktree list`) for situational awareness and run the conflict check. **Do not remove other worktrees or branches at session start.** Destructive cleanup at every agent's bootup duplicates teardown and risks deleting another agent's in-flight work.
331|- **Session end, tear down your own.** After *your* PR merges, remove the worktree and delete the branch *you* created (see §Cleanup after PR merges). Each session cleans up after itself.
332|- **Orphan GC, one owner.** Worktrees/branches that are truly abandoned (remote `[gone]` **and** no open PR **and** not held by an active session) accumulate when a session aborts or a PR merges after its session has ended. These are garbage-collected in **one** place, **TRON-FLYNN's health check (C1)**, or by an intentional manual prune. Never as a per-session-start chore.
333|
334|```
335|git worktree remove ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
336|git branch -D {branch}
337|git worktree prune                       # drop admin entries for manually-deleted dirs
338|```
339|
340|---
341|
342|## Prohibited
343|
344|| Operation | Reason |
345||:--|:--|
346|| Edit files in main checkout | Violates invariant 1 |
347|| `git gc` / `git prune` while other agents active | Corrupts shared `.git` |
348|| `git push --force` | Use `--force-with-lease` instead |
349|| `gh pr merge --auto` | Auto-merge is banned |
350|| Branch without Linear ID | Breaks traceability |
351|
352|---
353|
354|## Project-specific extensions
355|
356|Each project defines in its local worktree skill:
357|- Integration branch name, declared at repo root in a tracked `.integration-branch` file (default `main`; e.g. `staging` for app repos that deploy from staging). Hooks read this file to know which branch to protect (`principles-base.md §14 Integration branch marker`).
358|- Repo name to use in worktree directory
359|- Any additional CI/PR requirements
360|
361|Worktree path is **not** project-overridable, it is fixed by `principles-base.md §14 Worktree path`. Legacy per-project paths (e.g. `~/Spaceship/{repo}--{branch}`) are no longer permitted; migrate via `scripts/setup-repo.sh` + `git worktree repair`.
362|
363|---
364|
365|**Last Updated:** 2026-09-09, Branches now carry a Linear ID, and planned work also carries phase and block IDs. Earlier 2026-06-16, Session-start made **read-only** (inspect + conflict check); destructive stale-worktree removal dropped from every-session bootup. Renamed §"Stale cleanup (every session, start and end)" → §"Worktree teardown & orphan GC", splitting three responsibilities: session-start (read-only), session-end (tear down your own), orphan GC (single owner = TRON-FLYNN C1). Earlier 2026-05-13, Path conventions added (multi-repo `{project}/worktrees/{repo}--{branch}/`, single-repo / canon `{repo}/.worktrees/{branch}/`); legacy per-project worktree base path removed (canon §14 is now the single source). Meta repos section added (direct push to `main` from worktree). {"content": "1|name: CI
2|
3|# What a contributor cannot run themselves, run for them. The last three pull
4|# requests here arrived with some version of "no automated check could be run
5|# against this repository, so this change is unverified" — the invariants in
6|# tools/check.js only ever ran on a maintainer's machine, and neither the author
7|# nor the reviewer saw them until after the fact.
8|on:
9|  push:
10|    branches: [main]
11|  pull_request:
12|  workflow_dispatch:
13|
14|# Nothing here writes anything back, and `pull_request` (never
15|# `pull_request_target`) is what keeps a fork's code away from anything it could
16|# write with: it runs from the merge ref with a read-only token and no secrets.
17|# The repository default is already read, but that is a settings toggle anyone
18|# with admin can flip; declaring it here is what pins it.
19|permissions:
20|  contents: read
21|
22|concurrency:
23|  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
24|  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
25|
26|jobs:
27|  check:
28|    name: invariants
29|    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
30|    timeout-minutes: 10
31|    steps:
32|      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
33|      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
34|        with:
35|          node-version: '20'
36|      - run: npm ci
37|      # The invariants: identity declarations, every script parses, the tab-bar
38|      # poll interval stays above its timeout, sidebar inks clear a contrast
39|      # floor, every glyph falls inside a mapped codepoint range, and the
40|      # workspace order settles instead of moving again on its own wake. Each
41|      # one is there because the thing it checks went wrong once.
42|      - run: npm run check
43|      # Behaviour, in test/: what has to be driven rather than read.
44|      - run: npm test
45|      # And that the invariants can fail: each known-bad shape is put back and
46|      # must turn the check red. A check that can only pass is not a check.
47|      - run: npm run prove
48|      - run: npx prettier --check .
49|
50|  font:
51|    name: font is not stale
52|    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
53|    timeout-minutes: 10
54|    steps:
55|      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
56|      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
57|        with:
58|          # tools/build_font.py reads tools/codepoints.toml with tomllib.
59|          python-version: '3.12'
60|      - run: pip install -r tools/requirements.txt

{"content": "1|---
2|name: skill-git-multi-agent

7|
8|# Skill: Git Workflow: Multi-Agent
9|
10|Single source of truth for Git workflow across all parallel-agent projects. Worktree lifecycle, branch flow, rebase, CI monitoring, and one-time portable-worktree setup. `skill-branching-strategy.md` remains canonical for its §Cross-Repo Ordering content; `skill-worktree-workflow.md` is fully superseded and now a stub.
11|
12|---
13|
14|## Invariants (never violated)
15|
16|1. **Main checkout always on the integration branch, before, during, and after every session.** Never a feature branch, never the deploy branch. Read-only: no edits, no commits, no staged files. Leave it on the integration branch when done.
17|2. **Every agent works in a worktree.** No exceptions, even for one-line changes.
18|3. **One worktree per branch.** Two agents never share a worktree.
19|4. **Every branch references a Linear ID.** Block work also references its phase and block ID.
20|5. **All PRs target the integration branch.** Only `hotfix/*` may bypass.
21|6. **Always rebase on the integration branch before pushing.** No exceptions, skipping causes out-of-date rejections and integration conflicts.
22|7. **Monitor CI after every push. Do not proceed until all checks are green.** Fix failures before any next step.
23|
24|---
25|
26|## One-time repo setup
27|
28|Required before adding any worktree. Apply once per clone (new or existing). Implements `principles-base.md §14 Portability, Relative-path worktrees`. Requires Git ≥ 2.48 on every machine that will touch the repo.
29|
30|Because `.git/config` is never tracked, this setup cannot be encoded as a tracked git artifact. The portable solution is a **tracked bootstrap script** copied from the kit's `templates/meta/scripts/setup-repo.sh` into each repo's `scripts/setup-repo.sh`, then wired into the package manager's install lifecycle so contributors don't have to remember to run it.
31|
32|### Canonical script
33|
34|The kit template at `templates/meta/scripts/setup-repo.sh` does the full sequence idempotently:
35|
36|```
37|git config core.repositoryformatversion 1   # only if currently 0
38|git config worktree.useRelativePaths true   # implicitly enables extensions.relativeWorktrees
39|git worktree repair                          # converts pre-existing worktrees; no-op otherwise
40|```
41|
42|It also guards on Git version (≥ 2.48), resolves to the repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, exits silently when not in a git context (so it can't break tarball installs), and prints a one-line confirmation. Copy the script body into the project unchanged, do not symlink across repos (defeats portability). The leading comment block and the final echo message may be project-localized; the executable body must remain functionally identical so any future fix to the canonical can be re-applied with `diff` confidence.
43|
44|### Wiring variants
45|
46|Pick the variant that matches the repo's package manager. The script must auto-run after a fresh clone for the rule to hold across machines.
47|
48|| Repo type | Wiring | Trigger |
49||:--|:--|:--|
50|| Node (npm / pnpm / yarn) | Add `"prepare": "./scripts/setup-repo.sh"` (or `"../scripts/setup-repo.sh"` if `package.json` is in a subdirectory) to the install-time package's `package.json`. | `npm install` / `pnpm install` |
51|| Python (poetry) | Add a `tool.poetry.scripts` entry or a `poetry run` invocation in the project's bootstrap doc; or use a `Makefile setup` target. | `poetry install` or `make setup` |
52|| Plain (no package manager) | Document `./scripts/setup-repo.sh` as the first step in the README "Setup" section. | Manual, once per clone |
53|| Multi-repo workspace (e.g. `lens-app/` + `lens-meta/`) | Each repo carries its own `scripts/setup-repo.sh`. The workspace-root `README.md` / `AGENTS.md` lists both. | One per repo |
54|
55|### Migration order matters
56|
57|If you ever apply the raw commands by hand (e.g. on a repo that can't run shell scripts), bump `core.repositoryformatversion` to `1` *before* enabling the extension or `useRelativePaths`. Setting the extension on a version-0 repo leaves Git unable to operate on it until the version is bumped.
58|
59|---
60|
61|## Setup (once per session)
62|
63|```
64|cd {main-checkout}
65|git checkout {integration-branch}        # verify — fix if wrong
66|git fetch --prune origin                 # prunes remote-tracking refs for deleted branches
67|git branch -vv                           # [gone] = orphaned; note it — do NOT remove here (TRON-FLYNN GC owns it)
68|git worktree list                        # inspect (read-only) — situational awareness, not cleanup
69|gh pr list --base {integration-branch} --state open   # conflict check
70|```
71|
72|Session start is **read-only**: verify your checkout, inspect, and run the conflict check, do not remove other worktrees/branches here (see §Worktree teardown & orphan GC). If any open PR touches your task's files → **stop, report to user**.
73|
74|---
75|
76|## Branch naming
77|
78|| Work type | Pattern | Example |
79||:--|:--|:--|
80|| Block work | `{type}/B{PP}-{BB}-L{NNN}-{slug}` | `feat/B06-13-L123-github-actions-ci` |
81|| Non-block work | `{type}/adhoc-L{NNN}-{slug}` | `fix/adhoc-L456-typo-in-faq` |
82|| Hotfix | `hotfix/B{PP}-{BB}-L{NNN}-{slug}` or `hotfix/adhoc-L{NNN}-{slug}` | `hotfix/adhoc-L789-broken-login-redirect` |
83|
84|Rules: type and slug lowercase · `B` and `L` uppercase · phase and block numbers each have at least two digits · Linear ID required on every branch · every task inside a block keeps its `B{PP}-{BB}` · `hotfix/` is the only type that may PR into the deploy branch.
85|

87|
88|## Worktree lifecycle
89|
90|### Path conventions
91|
92|Canonical: `principles-base.md §14 Worktree path`. Not project-overridable.
93|
94|| Repo class | Path | Example |
95||:--|:--|:--|
96|| Multi-repo project (canon-extended, app, meta, …) | `{project}/worktrees/{repo}--{branch}/` | `hiresling.ai/worktrees/hiresling-app--feat-B90-01-L123-drafts/` |
97|| Single-repo / canon (e.g. `tortuga/`) | `{repo}/.worktrees/{branch}/` (gitignored) | `tortuga/.worktrees/chore/adhoc-L456-agent-system/` |
98|
99|The code blocks below show the multi-repo flow as default. For single-repo / canon, substitute `../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}` with `.worktrees/{branch}` and `cd {main-checkout}` with `cd {repo}` (the main checkout *is* the repo root). Parent dirs (`worktrees/` or `.worktrees/{nested}/`) must exist before `git worktree add`, `mkdir -p` first if needed.
100|
101|### Create (new branch)
102|
103|```
104|cd {main-checkout}
105|git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} -b {branch} origin/{integration-branch}
106|cd ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
107|```
108|
109|### Resume (existing branch with open PR)
110|
111|If the branch exists locally:
112|
113|```
114|cd {main-checkout}
115|git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} {branch}
116|cd ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
117|git pull --ff-only origin {branch}
118|```
119|
120|If the branch only exists on origin (no local ref yet):
121|
122|```
123|cd {main-checkout}
124|git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} -b {branch} origin/{branch}
125|cd ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
126|```
127|
128|### Work
129|
130|All reads, edits, commits, and pushes happen **inside the worktree**. Never in the main checkout.
131|
132|Commit at each task boundary, not at session end.
133|
134|```
135|git add {files}
136|git commit -m "{type}({scope}): {description}"   # Conventional Commits
137|```
138|
139|### Push
140|
141|First push:
142|
143|```
144|git fetch origin
145|git rebase origin/{integration-branch}
146|git push -u origin {branch}
147|```
148|
149|Re-push after rebase or amend:
150|
151|```
152|git fetch origin
153|git rebase origin/{integration-branch}
154|git push --force-with-lease origin {branch}
155|```
156|
157|Rebase conflict during push:
158|
159|```
160|# resolve conflict in file(s)
161|git add {resolved-files}
162|git rebase --continue
163|git push --force-with-lease origin {branch}
164|```
165|
166|### Monitor CI
167|
168|```
169|gh pr checks {PR-number} --watch
170|```
171|
172|Do not open a PR, request review, or proceed to the next task until all checks pass. If any check fails → fix, commit, push, rebase, repeat.
173|
174|### Open PR
175|
176|```
177|gh pr create --base {integration-branch} --title "{commit subject}" --body "Block: {block-id}"
178|```
179|
180|### Cleanup (after PR merges)
181|
182|Confirm the PR is merged before running:
183|
184|```
185|gh pr view {PR-number} --json state --jq '.state'   # must return MERGED
186|cd {main-checkout}
187|git fetch --prune origin
188|git worktree remove ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
189|git branch -D {branch}
190|git pull --ff-only origin {integration-branch}
191|```

195|## Meta repos (`.repo-class=meta`)
196|
197|Meta repos (project knowledge bases, agent docs, logs, blocks) drop **only** the PR/staging ceremony, the worktree-mandatory rule still applies.

199|Flow:
200|
201|```
202|cd {main-checkout}                                # meta repo root
203|git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} -b {branch} origin/main
204|cd ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
205|# work + commit
206|git fetch origin
207|git rebase origin/main
208|git push origin {branch}:main                     # direct push to main
209|cd {main-checkout}
210|git worktree remove ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
211|git branch -D {branch}
212|git pull --ff-only origin main
213|```
214|
215|`.githooks/pre-push` template allows this when `.repo-class=meta`; for canon and app it enforces the PR flow.
216|
217|---
218|
219|## Hook enforcement
220|
221|A `.githooks/pre-commit` hook (kit template: `templates/meta/.githooks/pre-commit`, installed by `scripts/setup-repo.sh`) blocks any commit that did not originate from an added worktree. Applies to every `.repo-class` value (canon, meta, app). Detection: `git rev-parse --git-dir` lacking `.git/worktrees/` substring → fail.
222|
223|Hook failure message:
224|
225|```
226|✘ pre-commit blocked — commit must run in an added worktree, not the main checkout.
227|  Single-repo / canon:  git worktree add .worktrees/{branch} -b {branch} origin/main
228|  Multi-repo project:   git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} -b {branch} origin/{integration-branch}
229|```
230|
231|Bypassing with `--no-verify` violates Invariant 1 and `principles-base.md §14`.
232|
233|---
234|
235|## Hook integration patterns
236|
237|`.githooks/` is a **library of canon-prescribed scripts**, `pre-commit` and `pre-push` MUST fire on their respective events, but the dispatcher is the repo's choice. `scripts/setup-repo.sh` detects an existing dispatcher (`lefthook.yml`, `.husky/`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`) and skips the `core.hooksPath=.githooks` override (which would silently suppress the dispatcher's own `.git/hooks/` installation).
238|
239|Pick the pattern that matches your repo.
240|
241|### Pattern A: git native (default, no dispatcher)
242|
243|No `lefthook.yml` / `.husky/` / `.pre-commit-config.yaml` at repo root. `scripts/setup-repo.sh` sets `core.hooksPath=.githooks` and git invokes the canon scripts directly. Nothing else to wire.
244|
245|### Pattern B: lefthook
246|
247|Add to `lefthook.yml`:
248|
249|```yaml
250|pre-commit:
251|  commands:
252|    canon-pre-commit:
253|      run: bash .githooks/pre-commit
254|      fail_text: "Canon pre-commit failed (see principles-base.md §14)"
255|
256|pre-push:
257|  commands:
258|    canon-pre-push:
259|      run: bash .githooks/pre-push "$1" "$2"
260|      fail_text: "Canon pre-push failed (see principles-base.md §14)"
261|```
262|
263|**⚠ Re-install warning.** `lefthook install` writes dispatcher scripts into `.git/hooks/` and may also touch `core.hooksPath` depending on the lefthook version. After any `lefthook install`, run `scripts/setup-repo.sh` again so its dispatcher detection unsets a stale `core.hooksPath=.githooks` if one snuck back in. Order: `lefthook install` first, `setup-repo.sh` second.
264|
265|### Pattern C: husky
266|
267|`.husky/pre-commit`:
268|
269|```sh
270|#!/usr/bin/env sh
271|. "$(dirname -- "$0")/_/husky.sh"
272|bash .githooks/pre-commit
273|```
274|
275|`.husky/pre-push`:
276|
277|```sh
278|#!/usr/bin/env sh
279|. "$(dirname -- "$0")/_/husky.sh"
280|bash .githooks/pre-push "$@"
281|```
282|
283|`chmod +x .husky/pre-commit .husky/pre-push`. Husky installs into `.git/hooks/` on `husky install`; `setup-repo.sh` leaves `core.hooksPath` unset when `.husky/` is detected so husky's installation is not suppressed.
284|
285|### Pattern D: pre-commit-framework
286|
287|Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:
288|
289|```yaml
290|repos:
291|  - repo: local
292|    hooks:
293|      - id: canon-pre-commit
294|        name: Canon pre-commit (worktree + integration-branch guard)
295|        entry: bash .githooks/pre-commit
296|        language: system
297|        stages: [pre-commit]
298|        pass_filenames: false
299|      - id: canon-pre-push
300|        name: Canon pre-push (reachability check)
301|        entry: bash .githooks/pre-push
302|        language: system
303|        stages: [pre-push]
304|        pass_filenames: false
305|```
306|
307|Run `pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push` after editing. Same caveat as lefthook: after any re-install, re-run `scripts/setup-repo.sh`.
308|
309|### Verifying wire-up
310|
311|After any wire-up change, validate from the main checkout AND from an added worktree:
312|
313|```sh
314|# In main checkout — pre-commit must FAIL:
315|git commit --allow-empty -m "verify: should-fail"
316|
317|# In a worktree off the integration branch — pre-commit must PASS:
318|git worktree add .worktrees/verify -b chore/adhoc-L123-verify-wireup origin/main  # or origin/staging for apps
319|cd .worktrees/verify && git commit --allow-empty -m "verify: should-pass"
320|```
321|
322|If both behave correctly, the canon scripts are firing through the chosen dispatcher.
323|
324|---
325|
326|## Worktree teardown & orphan GC
327|
328|Three distinct responsibilities, do not conflate them:
329|
330|- **Session start, read-only.** Inspect (`git branch -vv`, `git worktree list`) for situational awareness and run the conflict check. **Do not remove other worktrees or branches at session start.** Destructive cleanup at every agent's bootup duplicates teardown and risks deleting another agent's in-flight work.
331|- **Session end, tear down your own.** After *your* PR merges, remove the worktree and delete the branch *you* created (see §Cleanup after PR merges). Each session cleans up after itself.
332|- **Orphan GC, one owner.** Worktrees/branches that are truly abandoned (remote `[gone]` **and** no open PR **and** not held by an active session) accumulate when a session aborts or a PR merges after its session has ended. These are garbage-collected in **one** place, **TRON-FLYNN's health check (C1)**, or by an intentional manual prune. Never as a per-session-start chore.
333|
334|```
335|git worktree remove ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
336|git branch -D {branch}
337|git worktree prune                       # drop admin entries for manually-deleted dirs
338|```
339|
340|---
341|
342|## Prohibited
343|
344|| Operation | Reason |
345||:--|:--|
346|| Edit files in main checkout | Violates invariant 1 |
347|| `git gc` / `git prune` while other agents active | Corrupts shared `.git` |
348|| `git push --force` | Use `--force-with-lease` instead |
349|| `gh pr merge --auto` | Auto-merge is banned |
350|| Branch without Linear ID | Breaks traceability |
351|
352|---
353|
354|## Project-specific extensions
355|
356|Each project defines in its local worktree skill:
357|- Integration branch name, declared at repo root in a tracked `.integration-branch` file (default `main`; e.g. `staging` for app repos that deploy from staging). Hooks read this file to know which branch to protect (`principles-base.md §14 Integration branch marker`).
358|- Repo name to use in worktree directory
359|- Any additional CI/PR requirements
360|
361|Worktree path is **not** project-overridable, it is fixed by `principles-base.md §14 Worktree path`. Legacy per-project paths (e.g. `~/Spaceship/{repo}--{branch}`) are no longer permitted; migrate via `scripts/setup-repo.sh` + `git worktree repair`.
362|
363|---
364|
365|**Last Updated:** 2026-09-09, Branches now carry a Linear ID, and planned work also carries phase and block IDs. Earlier 2026-06-16, Session-start made **read-only** (inspect + conflict check); destructive stale-worktree removal dropped from every-session bootup. Renamed §"Stale cleanup (every session, start and end)" → §"Worktree teardown & orphan GC", splitting three responsibilities: session-start (read-only), session-end (tear down your own), orphan GC (single owner = TRON-FLYNN C1). Earlier 2026-05-13, Path conventions added (multi-repo `{project}/worktrees/{repo}--{branch}/`, single-repo / canon `{repo}/.worktrees/{branch}/`); legacy per-project worktree base path removed (canon §14 is now the single source). Meta repos section added (direct push to `main` from worktree). {"content": "1|name: CI
2|
3|# What a contributor cannot run themselves, run for them. The last three pull
4|# requests here arrived with some version of "no automated check could be run
5|# against this repository, so this change is unverified" — the invariants in
6|# tools/check.js only ever ran on a maintainer's machine, and neither the author
7|# nor the reviewer saw them until after the fact.
8|on:
9|  push:
10|    branches: [main]
11|  pull_request:
12|  workflow_dispatch:
13|
14|# Nothing here writes anything back, and `pull_request` (never
15|# `pull_request_target`) is what keeps a fork's code away from anything it could
16|# write with: it runs from the merge ref with a read-only token and no secrets.
17|# The repository default is already read, but that is a settings toggle anyone
18|# with admin can flip; declaring it here is what pins it.
19|permissions:
20|  contents: read
21|
22|concurrency:
23|  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
24|  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
25|
26|jobs:
27|  check:
28|    name: invariants
29|    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
30|    timeout-minutes: 10
31|    steps:
32|      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
33|      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
34|        with:
35|          node-version: '20'
36|      - run: npm ci
37|      # The invariants: identity declarations, every script parses, the tab-bar
38|      # poll interval stays above its timeout, sidebar inks clear a contrast
39|      # floor, every glyph falls inside a mapped codepoint range, and the
40|      # workspace order settles instead of moving again on its own wake. Each
41|      # one is there because the thing it checks went wrong once.
42|      - run: npm run check
43|      # Behaviour, in test/: what has to be driven rather than read.
44|      - run: npm test
45|      # And that the invariants can fail: each known-bad shape is put back and
46|      # must turn the check red. A check that can only pass is not a check.
47|      - run: npm run prove
48|      - run: npx prettier --check .
49|
50|  font:
51|    name: font is not stale
52|    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
53|    timeout-minutes: 10
54|    steps:
55|      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
56|      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
57|        with:
58|          # tools/build_font.py reads tools/codepoints.toml with tomllib.
59|          python-version: '3.12'
60|      - run: pip install -r tools/requirements.txt
61|      # dist/*.ttf is committed and build_patched_font.py says the patched face
62|      # "goes stale silently" — edit a mark or a codepoint, forget to rebuild,
63|      # and every install afterwards ships the old glyphs with no error
64|      # anywhere.
65|      #
66|      # The icon font is byte-reproducible (FONT_TIMESTAMP is fixed for exactly
67|      # this) as long as fontTools does not move under it, which is why
68|      # requirements.txt pins rather than floors it — so rebuilding and diffing
69|      # it is an exact test. The patched face is not reproducible at all: two consecutive builds of it differ, so a byte diff there would
70|      # fail on every run and teach everyone to ignore this job. It carries its
71|      # own answer instead — build_patched_font.py stamps nameID 3 with a hash
72|      # of the icon font it copied from, so comparing that stamp against the
73|      # icon font is precise and needs no rebuild at all.
74|      - run: python tools/build_font.py
75|      - name: Icon font matches a rebuild
76|        run: |
77|          if ! git diff --quiet -- dist/HerdrAgentIconsMax-Regular.ttf; then
78|            echo "::error::dist/HerdrAgentIconsMax-Regular.ttf is stale — run tools/build_font.py and commit dist/"
79|            exit 1
80|          fi
81|      - name: Patched font was built from this icon font
82|        run: |
83|          python - <<'PY'
84|          import hashlib, sys
85|          from pathlib import Path
86|          from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
87|
88|          icons = Path("dist/HerdrAgentIconsMax-Regular.ttf")
89|          patched = Path("dist/JetBrainsMonoHerdr-Regular.ttf")
90|          want = hashlib.sha256(icons.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:8]
91|          got = None
92|          for record in TTFont(patched)["name"].names:
93|              if record.nameID == 3:
94|                  got = record.toUnicode().rsplit("; ", 1)[-1]
95|                  break
96|          if got != want:
97|              print(
98|                  f"::error::{patched} was built from icon font {got}, but the "
99|                  f"committed one is {want} — rerun tools/build_patched_font.py "
100|                  "and commit dist/"
101|              )
102|              sys.exit(1)
103|          print(f"patched font carries icon stamp {want}")
